# Pest Testing 4

## Documentation

Use `search-docs` for detailed Pest 4 patterns and documentation.

## Basic Usage

### Creating Tests

All tests must be written using Pest. Use `php artisan make:test --pest {name}`.

The `{name}` argument should include only the path and test name, but should not include the test suite.
- Incorrect: `php artisan make:test --pest Feature/SomeFeatureTest` will generate `tests/Feature/Feature/SomeFeatureTest.php`
- Correct: `php artisan make:test --pest SomeControllerTest` will generate `tests/Feature/SomeControllerTest.php`
- Incorrect: `php artisan make:test --pest --unit Unit/SomeServiceTest` will generate `tests/Unit/Unit/SomeServiceTest.php`
- Correct: `php artisan make:test --pest --unit SomeServiceTest` will generate `tests/Unit/SomeServiceTest.php`

### Test Organization

- Unit/Feature tests: `tests/Feature` and `tests/Unit` directories.
- Browser tests: `tests/Browser/` directory.
- Do NOT remove tests without approval - these are core application code.

### Basic Test Structure

Pest supports both `test()` and `it()` functions. Before writing new tests, check existing test files in the same directory to match the project's convention. Use `test()` if existing tests use `test()`, or `it()` if they use `it()`.

<!-- Basic Pest Test Example -->
```php
it('is true', function () {
    expect(true)->toBeTrue();
});
```

### Running Tests

- Run minimal tests with filter before finalizing: `php artisan test --compact --filter=testName`.
- Run all tests: `php artisan test --compact`.
- Run file: `php artisan test --compact tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php`.

## Assertions

Use specific assertions (`assertSuccessful()`, `assertNotFound()`) instead of `assertStatus()`:

<!-- Pest Response Assertion -->
```php
it('returns all', function () {
    $this->postJson('/api/docs', [])->assertSuccessful();
});
```

| Use | Instead of |
|-----|------------|
| `assertSuccessful()` | `assertStatus(200)` |
| `assertNotFound()` | `assertStatus(404)` |
| `assertForbidden()` | `assertStatus(403)` |

## Mocking

Import mock function before use: `use function Pest\Laravel\mock;`

## Datasets

Use datasets for repetitive tests (validation rules, etc.):

<!-- Pest Dataset Example -->
```php
it('has emails', function (string $email) {
    expect($email)->not->toBeEmpty();
})->with([
    'james' => 'james@laravel.com',
    'taylor' => 'taylor@laravel.com',
]);
```

## Pest 4 Features

| Feature | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| Browser Testing | Full integration tests in real browsers |
| Smoke Testing | Validate multiple pages quickly |
| Visual Regression | Compare screenshots for visual changes |
| Test Sharding | Parallel CI runs |
| Architecture Testing | Enforce code conventions |

### Browser Test Example

Browser tests run in real browsers for full integration testing:

- Browser tests live in `tests/Browser/`.
- Use Laravel features like `Event::fake()`, `assertAuthenticated()`, and model factories.
- Use `RefreshDatabase` for clean state per test.
- Interact with page: click, type, scroll, select, submit, drag-and-drop, touch gestures.
- Test on multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) if requested.
- Test on different devices/viewports (iPhone 14 Pro, tablets) if requested.
- Switch color schemes (light/dark mode) when appropriate.
- Take screenshots or pause tests for debugging.

<!-- Pest Browser Test Example -->
```php
it('may reset the password', function () {
    Notification::fake();

    $this->actingAs(User::factory()->create());

    $page = visit('/sign-in');

    $page->assertSee('Sign In')
        ->assertNoJavaScriptErrors()
        ->click('Forgot Password?')
        ->fill('email', 'nuno@laravel.com')
        ->click('Send Reset Link')
        ->assertSee('We have emailed your password reset link!');

    Notification::assertSent(ResetPassword::class);
});
```

### Smoke Testing

Quickly validate multiple pages have no JavaScript errors:

<!-- Pest Smoke Testing Example -->
```php
$pages = visit(['/', '/about', '/contact']);

$pages->assertNoJavaScriptErrors()->assertNoConsoleLogs();
```

### Visual Regression Testing

Capture and compare screenshots to detect visual changes.

### Test Sharding

Split tests across parallel processes for faster CI runs.

### Architecture Testing

Pest 4 includes architecture testing (from Pest 3):

<!-- Architecture Test Example -->
```php
arch('controllers')
    ->expect('App\Http\Controllers')
    ->toExtendNothing()
    ->toHaveSuffix('Controller');
```

## Common Pitfalls

- Not importing `use function Pest\Laravel\mock;` before using mock
- Using `assertStatus(200)` instead of `assertSuccessful()`
- Forgetting datasets for repetitive validation tests
- Deleting tests without approval
- Forgetting `assertNoJavaScriptErrors()` in browser tests
- Prefixing `Feature/` or `Unit/` in `{name}` when using `make:test`

# Tailwind CSS Development

## Documentation

Use `search-docs` for detailed Tailwind CSS v4 patterns and documentation.

## Basic Usage

- Use Tailwind CSS classes to style HTML. Check and follow existing Tailwind conventions in the project before introducing new patterns.
- Offer to extract repeated patterns into components that match the project's conventions (e.g., Blade, JSX, Vue).
- Consider class placement, order, priority, and defaults. Remove redundant classes, add classes to parent or child elements carefully to reduce repetition, and group elements logically.

## Tailwind CSS v4 Specifics

- Always use Tailwind CSS v4 and avoid deprecated utilities.
- `corePlugins` is not supported in Tailwind v4.

### CSS-First Configuration

In Tailwind v4, configuration is CSS-first using the `@theme` directive — no separate `tailwind.config.js` file is needed:

<!-- CSS-First Config -->
```css
@theme {
  --color-brand: oklch(0.72 0.11 178);
}
```

### Import Syntax

In Tailwind v4, import Tailwind with a regular CSS `@import` statement instead of the `@tailwind` directives used in v3:

<!-- v4 Import Syntax -->
```diff
- @tailwind base;
- @tailwind components;
- @tailwind utilities;
+ @import "tailwindcss";
```

### Replaced Utilities

Tailwind v4 removed deprecated utilities. Use the replacements shown below. Opacity values remain numeric.

| Deprecated | Replacement |
|------------|-------------|
| bg-opacity-* | bg-black/* |
| text-opacity-* | text-black/* |
| border-opacity-* | border-black/* |
| divide-opacity-* | divide-black/* |
| ring-opacity-* | ring-black/* |
| placeholder-opacity-* | placeholder-black/* |
| flex-shrink-* | shrink-* |
| flex-grow-* | grow-* |
| overflow-ellipsis | text-ellipsis |
| decoration-slice | box-decoration-slice |
| decoration-clone | box-decoration-clone |

## Spacing

Use `gap` utilities instead of margins for spacing between siblings:

<!-- Gap Utilities -->
```html
<div class="flex gap-8">
    <div>Item 1</div>
    <div>Item 2</div>
</div>
```

## Dark Mode

If existing pages and components support dark mode, new pages and components must support it the same way, typically using the `dark:` variant:

<!-- Dark Mode -->
```html
<div class="bg-white dark:bg-gray-900 text-gray-900 dark:text-white">
    Content adapts to color scheme
</div>
```

## Common Patterns

### Flexbox Layout

<!-- Flexbox Layout -->
```html
<div class="flex items-center justify-between gap-4">
    <div>Left content</div>
    <div>Right content</div>
</div>
```

### Grid Layout

<!-- Grid Layout -->
```html
<div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">
    <div>Card 1</div>
    <div>Card 2</div>
    <div>Card 3</div>
</div>
```

## Common Pitfalls

- Using deprecated v3 utilities (bg-opacity-*, flex-shrink-*, etc.)
- Using `@tailwind` directives instead of `@import "tailwindcss"`
- Trying to use `tailwind.config.js` instead of CSS `@theme` directive
- Using margins for spacing between siblings instead of gap utilities
- Forgetting to add dark mode variants when the project uses dark mode

# Wayfinder Development

## Documentation

Use `search-docs` for detailed Wayfinder patterns and documentation.

## Quick Reference

### Generate Routes

Run after route changes if Vite plugin isn't installed:
```bash
php artisan wayfinder:generate --no-interaction
```
For form helpers, use `--with-form` flag:
```bash
php artisan wayfinder:generate --with-form --no-interaction
```

### Import Patterns

<!-- Controller Action Imports -->
```typescript
// Named imports for tree-shaking (preferred)...
import { show, store, update } from '@/actions/App/Http/Controllers/PostController'

// Named route imports...
import { show as postShow } from '@/routes/post'
```

### Common Methods

<!-- Wayfinder Methods -->
```typescript
// Get route object...
show(1) // { url: "/posts/1", method: "get" }

// Get URL string...
show.url(1) // "/posts/1"

// Specific HTTP methods...
show.get(1)
store.post()
update.patch(1)
destroy.delete(1)

// Form attributes for HTML forms...
store.form() // { action: "/posts", method: "post" }

// Query parameters...
show(1, { query: { page: 1 } }) // "/posts/1?page=1"
```

## Wayfinder + Inertia

Use Wayfinder with the `<Form>` component:
<!-- Wayfinder Form (React) -->
```typescript
<Form {...store.form()}><input name="title" /></Form>
```

## Verification

1. Run `php artisan wayfinder:generate` to regenerate routes if Vite plugin isn't installed
2. Check TypeScript imports resolve correctly
3. Verify route URLs match expected paths

## Common Pitfalls

- Using default imports instead of named imports (breaks tree-shaking)
- Forgetting to regenerate after route changes
- Not using type-safe parameter objects for route model binding

        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240 # v2
        with:
          php-version: '8.4'
          tools: composer:v2
          coverage: none

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

        run: composer setup

        run: composer ci:check

  # UI-31: the §10 demo journey (docs/00-BUILD-BRIEF.md), driven end to end
  # against the real Docker stack — Postgres, Redis, MinIO, Mailpit, Horizon
  # actually processing jobs. Deliberately its own job, not a step in `ci`
  # above: it's slow by design (registers real tenants, sends real mail),
  # and a failure here means the product's own acceptance story is broken,
  # not a unit-level regression — worth seeing as a distinct, required
  # check rather than folded into the same signal as lint/types/Pest.
  e2e-acceptance:
    name: E2E acceptance suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Prepare environment file
        run: |
          cp .env.example .env
          APP_KEY="base64:$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
          sed -i "s|^APP_KEY=.*|APP_KEY=${APP_KEY}|" .env

      - name: Build and start the Docker stack
        run: docker compose up -d --build --wait

      - name: Install npm dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run the E2E acceptance suite
        run: npm run e2e:acceptance

      - name: Container logs (on failure)
        if: failure()
        run: docker compose logs --no-color

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-acceptance-report
          path: |
            playwright-report/
            test-results/
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Tear down the Docker stack
        if: always()
        run: docker compose down -v

=== boost rules ===

# Laravel Boost

## Tools

- Laravel Boost is an MCP server with tools designed specifically for this application. Prefer Boost tools over manual alternatives like shell commands or file reads.
- Use `database-query` to run read-only queries against the database instead of writing raw SQL in tinker.
- Use `database-schema` to inspect table structure before writing migrations or models.
- Use `get-absolute-url` to resolve the correct scheme, domain, and port for project URLs. Always use this before sharing a URL with the user.
- Use `browser-logs` to read browser logs, errors, and exceptions. Only recent logs are useful, ignore old entries.

## Searching Documentation (IMPORTANT)

- Always use `search-docs` before making code changes. Do not skip this step. It returns version-specific docs based on installed packages automatically.
- Pass a `packages` array to scope results when you know which packages are relevant.
- Use multiple broad, topic-based queries: `['rate limiting', 'routing rate limiting', 'routing']`. Expect the most relevant results first.
- Do not add package names to queries because package info is already shared. Use `test resource table`, not `filament 4 test resource table`.

### Search Syntax

1. Use words for auto-stemmed AND logic: `rate limit` matches both "rate" AND "limit".
2. Use `"quoted phrases"` for exact position matching: `"infinite scroll"` requires adjacent words in order.
3. Combine words and phrases for mixed queries: `middleware "rate limit"`.
4. Use multiple queries for OR logic: `queries=["authentication", "middleware"]`.

## Artisan

- Run Artisan commands directly via the command line (e.g., `php artisan route:list`). Use `php artisan list` to discover available commands and `php artisan [command] --help` to check parameters.
- Inspect routes with `php artisan route:list`. Filter with: `--method=GET`, `--name=users`, `--path=api`, `--except-vendor`, `--only-vendor`.
- Read configuration values using dot notation: `php artisan config:show app.name`, `php artisan config:show database.default`. Or read config files directly from the `config/` directory.

## Tinker

- Execute PHP in app context for debugging and testing code. Do not create models without user approval, prefer tests with factories instead. Prefer existing Artisan commands over custom tinker code.
- Always use single quotes to prevent shell expansion: `php artisan tinker --execute 'Your::code();'`
  - Double quotes for PHP strings inside: `php artisan tinker --execute 'User::where("active", true)->count();'`

=== inertia-laravel/core rules ===

# Inertia

- Inertia creates fully client-side rendered SPAs without modern SPA complexity, leveraging existing server-side patterns.
- Components live in `resources/js/pages` (unless specified in `vite.config.js`). Use `Inertia::render()` for server-side routing instead of Blade views.
- ALWAYS use `search-docs` tool for version-specific Inertia documentation and updated code examples.
- IMPORTANT: Activate `inertia-react-development` when working with Inertia client-side patterns.

# Inertia v3

- Use all Inertia features from v1, v2, and v3. Check the documentation before making changes to ensure the correct approach.
- New v3 features: standalone HTTP requests (`useHttp` hook), optimistic updates with automatic rollback, layout props (`useLayoutProps` hook), instant visits, simplified SSR via `@inertiajs/vite` plugin, custom exception handling for error pages.
- Carried over from v2: deferred props, infinite scroll, merging props, polling, prefetching, once props, flash data.
- When using deferred props, add an empty state with a pulsing or animated skeleton.
- Axios has been removed. Use the built-in XHR client with interceptors, or install Axios separately if needed.
- `Inertia::lazy()` / `LazyProp` has been removed. Use `Inertia::optional()` instead.
- Prop types (`Inertia::optional()`, `Inertia::defer()`, `Inertia::merge()`) work inside nested arrays with dot-notation paths.
- SSR works automatically in Vite dev mode with `@inertiajs/vite` - no separate Node.js server needed during development.
- Event renames: `invalid` is now `httpException`, `exception` is now `networkError`.
- `router.cancel()` replaced by `router.cancelAll()`.
- The `future` configuration namespace has been removed - all v2 future options are now always enabled.

==================== ./app/Actions/Fortify/CreateNewUser.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Fortify;

use App\Concerns\PasswordValidationRules;
use App\Concerns\ProfileValidationRules;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;
use Laravel\Fortify\Contracts\CreatesNewUsers;

class CreateNewUser implements CreatesNewUsers
{
    use PasswordValidationRules, ProfileValidationRules;

    /**
     * Validate and create a newly registered user.
     *
     * @param  array<string, string>  $input
     */
    public function create(array $input): User
    {
        Validator::make($input, [
            ...$this->profileRules(),
            'password' => $this->passwordRules(),
        ])->validate();

        return User::create([
            'name' => $input['name'],
            'email' => $input['email'],
            'password' => $input['password'],
        ]);
    }
}


==================== ./app/Actions/Fortify/ResetUserPassword.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Actions\Fortify;

use App\Concerns\PasswordValidationRules;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;
use Laravel\Fortify\Contracts\ResetsUserPasswords;

class ResetUserPassword implements ResetsUserPasswords
{
    use PasswordValidationRules;

    /**
     * Validate and reset the user's forgotten password.
     *
     * @param  array<string, string>  $input
     */
    public function reset(User $user, array $input): void
    {
        Validator::make($input, [
            'password' => $this->passwordRules(),
        ])->validate();

        $user->forceFill([
            'password' => $input['password'],
        ])->save();
    }
}


==================== ./app/Concerns/PasswordValidationRules.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Concerns;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Validation\ValidationRule;
use Illuminate\Validation\Rules\Password;

trait PasswordValidationRules
{
    /**
     * Get the validation rules used to validate passwords.
     *
     * @return array<int, Password|ValidationRule|array<mixed>|string>
     */
    protected function passwordRules(): array
    {
        return ['required', 'string', Password::default(), 'confirmed'];
    }

    /**
     * Get the validation rules used to validate the current password.
     *
     * @return array<int, Password|ValidationRule|array<mixed>|string>
     */
    protected function currentPasswordRules(): array
    {
        return ['required', 'string', 'current_password'];
    }
}


==================== ./app/Concerns/ProfileValidationRules.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Concerns;

use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Validation\ValidationRule;
use Illuminate\Validation\Rule;

trait ProfileValidationRules
{
    /**
     * Get the validation rules used to validate user profiles.
     *
     * @return array<string, array<int, ValidationRule|array<mixed>|string>>
     */
    protected function profileRules(?string $userId = null): array
    {
        return [
            'name' => $this->nameRules(),
            'email' => $this->emailRules($userId),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Get the validation rules used to validate user names.
     *
     * @return array<int, ValidationRule|array<mixed>|string>
     */
    protected function nameRules(): array
    {
        return ['required', 'string', 'max:255'];
    }

    /**
     * Get the validation rules used to validate user emails.
     *
     * @return array<int, ValidationRule|array<mixed>|string>
     */
    protected function emailRules(?string $userId = null): array
    {
        return [
            'required',
            'string',
            'email',
            'max:255',
            $userId === null
                ? Rule::unique(User::class)
                : Rule::unique(User::class)->ignore($userId),
        ];
    }
}

namespace App\Console\Commands;

==================== ./app/Console/Commands/DetectAlerts.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Console\Commands;

use App\Domain\Inventory\Actions\DetectAlertsAction;
use App\Domain\Tenancy\Models\Tenant;
use Illuminate\Console\Command;

/**
 * Scheduled in routes/console.php. Runs detection tenant by tenant — each
 * iteration binds that tenant as current so BelongsToTenant/RLS apply
 * exactly as they would for a real request.
 */
class DetectAlerts extends Command
{
    protected $signature = 'alerts:detect';

    protected $description = 'Detect low-stock, near-expiry, and expired-batch alerts for every tenant';

    public function handle(DetectAlertsAction $action): int
    {
        Tenant::query()->each(function (Tenant $tenant) use ($action) {
            $tenant->makeCurrent();
            $opened = $action->execute($tenant);
            Tenant::forgetCurrent();

            $this->line("{$tenant->name}: {$opened['low_stock']} low-stock, {$opened['near_expiry']} near-expiry, {$opened['expired']} expired");
        });

        return self::SUCCESS;
    }
}


==================== ./app/Console/Commands/ExpireDataExports.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Console\Commands;

use App\Domain\Reporting\Actions\ExpireDataExportsAction;
use App\Domain\Tenancy\Models\Tenant;
use App\Support\Tenancy\TenantContext;
use Illuminate\Console\Command;

/**
 * Scheduled in routes/console.php. Reclaims the S3 object for any
 * completed export past its GenerateDataExportJob::RETENTION_DAYS window
 * and flips the row to Expired, so the history screen stops offering a
 * download button that would otherwise 410 on click.
 *
 * data_export_requests has a Postgres RLS policy (unlike alerts/digest
 * subscriptions), so this needs the full TenantContext::run() — makeCurrent()
 * alone satisfies Eloquent's TenantScope but leaves the RLS session
 * variable unset, which fails the query closed at the database level.
 */
class ExpireDataExports extends Command
{
    protected $signature = 'data-exports:expire';

    protected $description = 'Expire and delete data export archives past their retention window, for every tenant';

    public function handle(ExpireDataExportsAction $action): int
    {
        Tenant::query()->each(function (Tenant $tenant) use ($action) {
            $count = TenantContext::run($tenant, fn () => $action->execute($tenant));

            if ($count > 0) {
                $this->line("{$tenant->name}: expired {$count} data export(s)");
            }
        });

        return self::SUCCESS;
    }
}


==================== ./app/Console/Commands/SeedPilotVolume.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Console\Commands;

use App\Domain\Tenancy\Models\Tenant;
use Closure;
use Illuminate\Console\Command;
use Illuminate\Database\Connection;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

/**
 * S5-ANA-04 (performance): generates a synthetic pilot-scale dataset for
 * one tenant to measure real query performance against — CLAUDE.md's
 * targets ("common screens < 2s; evidence search < 2s at pilot volume")
 * don't define an exact row count, so this picks a concrete, documented
 * scale (~1 year of a busy single-practice pilot) rather than leaving
 * "pilot volume" untested against any real number:
 *   3 devices, 3,000 cycles, ~10 pouches/cycle (30,000 labels/usages),
 *   2,000 patients, 500 batches.
 *
 * Bulk-inserts via the admin connection (bypasses RLS — appropriate for a
 * one-off fixture script, never for request-serving code) since this is
 * a fixture generator, not a feature — CLAUDE.md's "demo/pilot datasets
 * fully synthetic" applies here regardless.
 */
class SeedPilotVolume extends Command
{
    protected $signature = 'steriqore:seed-pilot-volume {--force}';

    protected $description = 'Seed a synthetic pilot-scale dataset for one tenant (performance testing only)';

    private const CYCLE_COUNT = 3000;

    private const ITEMS_PER_CYCLE = 10;

    private const PATIENT_COUNT = 2000;

    private const BATCH_COUNT = 500;

    // Postgres caps a single query at 65,535 bind parameters — with
    // ITEMS_PER_CYCLE=10 rows per cycle and ~9 columns on the widest
    // table, the outer chunk has to stay well under 1,000 cycles.
    private const CHUNK_SIZE = 500;

    public function handle(): int
    {
        if (app()->isProduction() && ! $this->option('force')) {
            $this->error('Refusing to seed synthetic pilot-volume data in production without --force.');

            return self::FAILURE;
        }

        $db = DB::connection('pgsql_admin');
        $now = now();

        $this->line('Creating tenant, site, location, device, product, supplier...');
        $tenant = Tenant::create(['name' => 'Pilot Volume Clinic', 'slug' => 'pilot-volume-'.Str::lower(Str::random(8))]);
        $tenantId = $tenant->id;

        $siteId = (string) Str::uuid7();
        $db->table('sites')->insert(['id' => $siteId, 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'name' => 'Cabinet Principal', 'timezone' => 'Europe/Paris', 'is_primary' => true, 'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now]);

        $locationId = (string) Str::uuid7();
        $db->table('storage_locations')->insert(['id' => $locationId, 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'site_id' => $siteId, 'name' => 'Réserve', 'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now]);

        $userId = (string) Str::uuid7();
        $db->table('users')->insert(['id' => $userId, 'name' => 'Pilot Practitioner', 'email' => 'pilot-'.Str::lower(Str::random(8)).'@example.com', 'password' => Hash::make('password'), 'email_verified_at' => $now, 'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now]);
        $db->table('tenant_user')->insert(['id' => (string) Str::uuid7(), 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'user_id' => $userId, 'status' => 'active', 'joined_at' => $now, 'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now]);

        $categoryId = (string) Str::uuid7();
        $db->table('product_categories')->insert(['id' => $categoryId, 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'name' => 'Instruments', 'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now]);
        $productId = (string) Str::uuid7();
        $db->table('products')->insert(['id' => $productId, 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'category_id' => $categoryId, 'name' => 'Sachet de stérilisation', 'reference' => 'REF-PILOT', 'unit' => 'piece', 'min_threshold' => 0, 'is_sterilizable' => true, 'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now]);
        $supplierId = (string) Str::uuid7();
        $db->table('suppliers')->insert(['id' => $supplierId, 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'name' => 'Pilot Supplier', 'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now]);

        $deviceIds = [];
        for ($d = 0; $d < 3; $d++) {
            $deviceId = (string) Str::uuid7();
            $deviceIds[] = $deviceId;
            $db->table('devices')->insert(['id' => $deviceId, 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'site_id' => $siteId, 'name' => "Autoclave {$d}", 'serial_number' => "SN-PILOT-{$d}", 'kind' => 'autoclave', 'status' => 'active', 'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now]);
        }

        $dluRuleId = (string) Str::uuid7();
        $db->table('dlu_rules')->insert(['id' => $dluRuleId, 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'packaging_type' => 'Sachet', 'storage_condition' => 'Armoire', 'shelf_life_days' => 180, 'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now]);

        $this->line('Creating '.self::BATCH_COUNT.' batches...');
        $batchIds = $this->bulkInsert($db, 'batches', self::BATCH_COUNT, fn (int $i) => [
            'id' => (string) Str::uuid7(), 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'product_id' => $productId, 'supplier_id' => $supplierId,
            'batch_number' => "B-{$i}", 'expiry_date' => $now->clone()->addYear()->toDateString(), 'received_at' => $now, 'status' => 'active',
            'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now,
        ]);

        $this->line('Creating '.self::PATIENT_COUNT.' patients...');
        $patientIds = $this->bulkInsert($db, 'patients', self::PATIENT_COUNT, fn (int $i) => [
            'id' => (string) Str::uuid7(), 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'reference' => 'PAT-'.str_pad((string) ($i + 1), 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT),
            'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now,
        ]);

        $this->line('Creating '.self::CYCLE_COUNT.' cycles with '.self::ITEMS_PER_CYCLE.' pouches each...');
        $cycleNumbersByDevice = [0, 0, 0];
        $progressBar = $this->output->createProgressBar(self::CYCLE_COUNT);

        for ($batchStart = 0; $batchStart < self::CYCLE_COUNT; $batchStart += self::CHUNK_SIZE) {
            $cycleRows = [];
            $itemRows = [];
            $labelRows = [];
            $usageRows = [];

            $batchEnd = min($batchStart + self::CHUNK_SIZE, self::CYCLE_COUNT);
            for ($c = $batchStart; $c < $batchEnd; $c++) {
                $deviceIndex = $c % 3;
                $deviceId = $deviceIds[$deviceIndex];
                $cycleNumbersByDevice[$deviceIndex]++;

                $cycleId = (string) Str::uuid7();
                $startedAt = $now->clone()->subDays(self::CYCLE_COUNT - $c);
                $completedAt = $startedAt->clone()->addMinutes(45);

                $cycleRows[] = [
                    'id' => $cycleId, 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'device_id' => $deviceId,
                    'operator_id' => $userId, 'cycle_number' => $cycleNumbersByDevice[$deviceIndex],
                    'status' => 'released', 'started_at' => $startedAt, 'completed_at' => $completedAt,
                    'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now,
                ];

                for ($i = 1; $i <= self::ITEMS_PER_CYCLE; $i++) {
                    $itemId = (string) Str::uuid7();
                    $batchId = $batchIds[array_rand($batchIds)];
                    $itemRows[] = [
                        'id' => $itemId, 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'cycle_id' => $cycleId, 'batch_id' => $batchId,
                        'description' => 'Kit chirurgical', 'sequence_in_cycle' => $i, 'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now,
                    ];

                    $labelId = (string) Str::uuid7();
                    $useByDate = $completedAt->clone()->addDays(180);
                    $labelRows[] = [
                        'id' => $labelId, 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'cycle_item_id' => $itemId, 'status' => 'used',
                        'packaging_type' => 'Sachet', 'storage_condition' => 'Armoire', 'shelf_life_days' => 180,
                        'sterilized_at' => $completedAt, 'use_by_date' => $useByDate->toDateString(), 'print_counter' => 1,
                        'created_at' => $now, 'updated_at' => $now,
                    ];

                    $patientId = $patientIds[array_rand($patientIds)];
                    $usageRows[] = [
                        'id' => (string) Str::uuid7(), 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'label_id' => $labelId,
                        'patient_id' => $patientId, 'practitioner_id' => $userId, 'procedure' => 'Détartrage',
                        'used_at' => $completedAt->clone()->addHour(), 'created_at' => $now,
                    ];
                }

                $progressBar->advance();
            }

            $db->table('cycles')->insert($cycleRows);
            $db->table('cycle_items')->insert($itemRows);
            $db->table('labels')->insert($labelRows);
            $db->table('label_usages')->insert($usageRows);
        }

        $progressBar->finish();
        $this->newLine(2);

        $releaseRows = $db->table('cycles')->where('tenant_id', $tenantId)->pluck('id')->map(fn ($cycleId) => [
            'id' => (string) Str::uuid7(), 'tenant_id' => $tenantId, 'cycle_id' => $cycleId, 'decision' => 'compliant',
            'released_by_user_id' => $userId, 'released_at' => $now, 'created_at' => $now,
        ])->all();
        foreach (array_chunk($releaseRows, self::CHUNK_SIZE) as $chunk) {
            $db->table('cycle_releases')->insert($chunk);
        }

        $this->info("Done. Tenant slug: {$tenant->slug}");

        return self::SUCCESS;
    }

    /**
     * @param  Closure(int): array<string, mixed>  $rowFactory
     * @return array<int, string> the generated ids
     */
    private function bulkInsert(Connection $connection, string $table, int $count, Closure $rowFactory): array
    {
        $ids = [];
        for ($start = 0; $start < $count; $start += self::CHUNK_SIZE) {
            $rows = [];
            $end = min($start + self::CHUNK_SIZE, $count);
            for ($i = $start; $i < $end; $i++) {
                $row = $rowFactory($i);
                $ids[] = $row['id'];
                $rows[] = $row;
            }
            $connection->table($table)->insert($rows);
        }

        return $ids;
    }
}


==================== ./app/Console/Commands/SendDigests.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Console\Commands;

use App\Domain\Identity\Actions\ResolveTenantUsersWithRoleAction;
use App\Domain\Inventory\Enums\AlertState;
use App\Domain\Inventory\Mail\DigestMail;
use App\Domain\Inventory\Models\Alert;
use App\Domain\Inventory\Models\AlertSettings;
use App\Domain\Inventory\Models\DigestSubscription;
use App\Domain\Tenancy\Models\Tenant;
use Illuminate\Console\Command;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Mail;

/**
 * Scheduled in routes/console.php. Runs tenant by tenant, same
 * makeCurrent()/forgetCurrent() pattern as DetectAlerts — every query here
 * already qualifies tenant_id explicitly, it doesn't rely on RLS session
 * scoping. Recipients are resolved live from whoever currently holds the
 * subscribed role (DigestSubscription's own docblock), never a stored
 * address list, so this stays correct as team membership (UI-26) changes.
 */
class SendDigests extends Command
{
    protected $signature = 'digests:send';

    protected $description = 'Send the alerts digest to every due, subscribed role in every tenant';

    public function __construct(private ResolveTenantUsersWithRoleAction $resolveUsersWithRole)
    {
        parent::__construct();
    }

    public function handle(): int
    {
        Tenant::query()->each(function (Tenant $tenant) {
            $tenant->makeCurrent();

            $settings = AlertSettings::forTenant($tenant);

            if (! $settings->digests_enabled) {
                Tenant::forgetCurrent();

                return;
            }

            $openAlerts = Alert::where('tenant_id', $tenant->id)->where('state', AlertState::Open)->get();

            DigestSubscription::where('tenant_id', $tenant->id)
                ->where('enabled', true)
                ->each(function (DigestSubscription $subscription) use ($tenant, $openAlerts) {
                    if (! $this->isDue($subscription) || $openAlerts->isEmpty()) {
                        return;
                    }

                    $recipients = $this->resolveUsersWithRole->execute($tenant, $subscription->role);

                    foreach ($recipients as $recipient) {
                        Mail::to($recipient->email)->queue(new DigestMail($recipient, $tenant, $openAlerts));
                    }

                    $subscription->update(['last_sent_at' => now()]);
                    $this->line("{$tenant->name}: sent {$subscription->role} digest to {$recipients->count()} recipient(s)");
                });

            Tenant::forgetCurrent();
        });

        return self::SUCCESS;
    }

    private function isDue(DigestSubscription $subscription): bool
    {
        if ($subscription->last_sent_at === null) {
            return true;
        }

        return match ($subscription->frequency) {
            'weekly' => $subscription->last_sent_at->lt(now()->subWeek()),
            default => $subscription->last_sent_at->lt(now()->subDay()),
        };
    }
}


==================== ./app/Domain/Catalog/Actions/CreateProductAction.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Catalog\Actions;

use App\Domain\Catalog\Models\Product;
use App\Domain\Compliance\Actions\RecordAuditEventAction;
use App\Domain\Tenancy\Models\Tenant;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Support\Api\ApiException;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class CreateProductAction
{
    public function __construct(
        private RecordAuditEventAction $recordAuditEvent,
        private Request $request,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  array<string, mixed>  $attributes
     */
    public function execute(Tenant $tenant, User $actor, array $attributes): Product
    {
        if (Product::where('reference', $attributes['reference'])->exists()) {
            throw new ApiException('PRODUCT_REFERENCE_TAKEN', 'A product with this reference already exists.', 409);
        }

        $product = Product::create($attributes + ['tenant_id' => $tenant->id]);
        // Columns not in $attributes (unit, min_threshold, is_sterilizable)
        // fall back to their DB-level defaults, which the in-memory model
        // never sees unless re-read.
        $product->refresh();

        $this->recordAuditEvent->execute(
            tenant: $tenant,
            actor: $actor,
            action: 'product.created',
            subjectType: Product::class,
            subjectId: $product->id,
            newValues: $attributes,
            request: $this->request,
        );

        return $product;
    }
}

==================== ./app/Domain/Catalog/Actions/UpdateProductAction.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Catalog\Actions;

use App\Domain\Catalog\Models\Product;
use App\Domain\Compliance\Actions\RecordAuditEventAction;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Support\Api\ApiException;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class UpdateProductAction
{
    public function __construct(
        private RecordAuditEventAction $recordAuditEvent,
        private Request $request,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  array<string, mixed>  $attributes
     */
    public function execute(Product $product, User $actor, array $attributes): Product
    {
        if (
            isset($attributes['reference'])
            && Product::where('reference', $attributes['reference'])->where('id', '!=', $product->id)->exists()
        ) {
            throw new ApiException('PRODUCT_REFERENCE_TAKEN', 'A product with this reference already exists.', 409);
        }

        $oldValues = $product->only(array_keys($attributes));
        $product->update($attributes);

        $this->recordAuditEvent->execute(
            tenant: $product->tenant,
            actor: $actor,
            action: 'product.updated',
            subjectType: Product::class,
            subjectId: $product->id,
            oldValues: $oldValues,
            newValues: $attributes,
            request: $this->request,
        );

        return $product;
    }
}

<?php

==================== ./app/Domain/Compliance/Actions/MirrorMediaBackupAction.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Compliance\Actions;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;

/**
 * spatie/laravel-backup only zips local paths — the real user-generated
 * files (cycle attachments, etc.) live on the 'media' S3 disk, so REC-10
 * ("restore PG + S3 backup") needs its own mechanism. Every object is
 * copied to the 'backups' disk under media-backup/, preserving its path,
 * so RestoreMediaBackupAction can copy it straight back.
 */
class MirrorMediaBackupAction
{
    private const string PREFIX = 'media-backup';

    /**
     * @return int number of files mirrored
     */
    public function execute(): int
    {
        $count = 0;

        foreach (Storage::disk('media')->allFiles() as $path) {
            Storage::disk('backups')->put(
                self::PREFIX.'/'.$path,
                Storage::disk('media')->get($path),
            );
            $count++;
        }

        return $count;
    }
}


==================== ./app/Domain/Compliance/Actions/RaiseNonConformityAction.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Compliance\Actions;

use App\Domain\Compliance\Models\NonConformity;
use App\Domain\Inventory\Enums\BatchStatus;
use App\Domain\Inventory\Models\Batch;
use App\Domain\Labeling\Enums\LabelStatus;
use App\Domain\Labeling\Models\Label;
use App\Domain\Sterilization\Models\Cycle;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Support\Dashboard\DashboardCache;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

/**
 * CLAUDE.md invariant #3: "Mistakes are corrected by a non_conformity +
 * recall, never by UPDATE." Never touches an evidence table (cycles,
 * releases, labels' own history, usages, movements, audit_events stay
 * exactly as they were) — only Label.status and Batch.status move,
 * which are mutable state-machine fields, not the evidence itself.
 */
class RaiseNonConformityAction
{
    public function __construct(
        private RecordAuditEventAction $recordAuditEvent,
        private Request $request,
    ) {}

    public function execute(Cycle|Label $subject, User $actor, string $description): NonConformity
    {
        return DB::transaction(function () use ($subject, $actor, $description) {
            $nonConformity = NonConformity::create([
                'tenant_id' => $subject->tenant_id,
                'subject_type' => $subject::class,
                'subject_id' => $subject->id,
                'description' => $description,
                'raised_by_user_id' => $actor->id,
                'raised_at' => now(),
            ]);

            $labels = $this->affectedLabels($subject);

            foreach ($labels as $label) {
                if (in_array($label->status, [LabelStatus::Recalled, LabelStatus::Voided], true)) {
                    continue;
                }

                $label->update(['status' => LabelStatus::Recalled]);

                $this->recordAuditEvent->execute(
                    tenant: $subject->tenant,
                    actor: $actor,
                    action: 'label.recalled',
                    subjectType: Label::class,
                    subjectId: $label->id,
                    reason: $description,
                    request: $this->request,
                );

                $batch = $label->cycleItem->batch;
                if ($batch instanceof Batch && $batch->status !== BatchStatus::Quarantined) {
                    $batch->update(['status' => BatchStatus::Quarantined]);

                    $this->recordAuditEvent->execute(
                        tenant: $subject->tenant,
                        actor: $actor,
                        action: 'batch.quarantined',
                        subjectType: Batch::class,
                        subjectId: $batch->id,
                        reason: $description,
                        request: $this->request,
                    );
                }
            }

            $this->recordAuditEvent->execute(
                tenant: $subject->tenant,
                actor: $actor,
                action: 'non_conformity.raised',
                subjectType: NonConformity::class,
                subjectId: $nonConformity->id,
                reason: $description,
                newValues: ['subject_type' => $subject::class, 'subject_id' => $subject->id],
                request: $this->request,
            );

            DashboardCache::forget($subject->tenant);

            return $nonConformity;
        });
    }

    /**
     * Read-only — the blast radius a confirmation screen shows BEFORE
     * raising, so the same skip conditions execute() applies (already-
     * recalled/voided labels, already-quarantined batches don't count
     * twice) must stay in sync with the loop above if either changes.
     *
     * @return array{labels_to_recall: int, batches_to_quarantine: int}
     */
    public function previewBlastRadius(Cycle|Label $subject): array
    {
        $labelsToRecall = $this->affectedLabels($subject)
            ->reject(fn (Label $label) => in_array($label->status, [LabelStatus::Recalled, LabelStatus::Voided], true));

        $batchesToQuarantine = $labelsToRecall
            ->map(fn (Label $label) => $label->cycleItem->batch)
            ->filter(fn ($batch) => $batch instanceof Batch && $batch->status !== BatchStatus::Quarantined)
            ->unique('id');

        return [
            'labels_to_recall' => $labelsToRecall->count(),
            'batches_to_quarantine' => $batchesToQuarantine->count(),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * @return Collection<int, Label>
     */
    public function affectedLabels(Cycle|Label $subject): Collection
    {
        if ($subject instanceof Label) {
            return new Collection([$subject]);
        }

        return Label::whereIn('cycle_item_id', $subject->items()->pluck('id'))->get();
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Compliance\Actions;

use App\Domain\Compliance\Models\AuditEvent;
use App\Domain\Tenancy\Models\Tenant;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

/**
 * The one place that writes to audit_events. Everything sensitive is
 * logged here: auth events, permission changes, releases, reprints,
 * recalls, adjustments, exports (CLAUDE.md's cross-cutting requirements).
 *
 * actor_label_snapshot is captured now, not read live off the user later —
 * a disabled or renamed user must not rewrite what past evidence says about
 * who did it (invariant #6).
 */
class RecordAuditEventAction
{
    /**
     * @param  array<string, mixed>|null  $oldValues
     * @param  array<string, mixed>|null  $newValues
     */
    public function execute(
        ?Tenant $tenant,
        ?User $actor,
        string $action,
        string $subjectType,
        string $subjectId,
        ?array $oldValues = null,
        ?array $newValues = null,
        ?string $reason = null,
        ?Request $request = null,
    ): AuditEvent {
        return AuditEvent::create([
            'tenant_id' => $tenant?->id,
            'actor_id' => $actor?->id,
            'actor_label_snapshot' => $actor ? "{$actor->name} <{$actor->email}>" : null,
            'action' => $action,
            'subject_type' => $subjectType,
            'subject_id' => $subjectId,
            'old_values' => $oldValues,
            'new_values' => $newValues,
            'reason' => $reason,
            'ip' => $request?->ip(),
            'user_agent' => $request?->userAgent(),
            'request_id' => $request?->attributes->get('request_id') ?? (string) Str::uuid7(),
            'occurred_at' => now(),
        ]);
    }
}

            'tenant_actual_id' => $tenantActual?->id,
            'route_name' => $this->request->route()?->getName(),
            'method' => $this->request->method(),
            'path' => $this->request->path(),
            'subject_type' => $subjectType,
            'subject_id' => $subjectId,
            'ip' => $this->request->ip(),
            'user_agent' => $this->request->userAgent(),
            'request_id' => $this->request->attributes->get('request_id') ?? (string) Str::uuid7(),
            'occurred_at' => now(),
        ]);
    }

==================== ./app/Domain/Compliance/Actions/ResolveNonConformityAction.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Compliance\Actions;

use App\Domain\Compliance\Models\NonConformity;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Support\Api\ApiException;
use App\Support\Dashboard\DashboardCache;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

/**
 * The "audited correction" — closing out a non-conformity with a note.
 * Does not un-recall labels or un-quarantine batches: those need their
 * own deliberate follow-up action once someone has actually verified the
 * pouch/batch is safe, which isn't something a resolution note alone can
 * assert.
 */
class ResolveNonConformityAction
{
    public function __construct(
        private RecordAuditEventAction $recordAuditEvent,
        private Request $request,
    ) {}

    public function execute(NonConformity $nonConformity, User $actor, string $resolution): NonConformity
    {
        if ($nonConformity->resolved_at !== null) {
            throw new ApiException('NON_CONFORMITY_ALREADY_RESOLVED', 'This non-conformity has already been resolved.', 409);
        }

        $nonConformity->update([
            'resolved_by_user_id' => $actor->id,
            'resolved_at' => now(),
            'resolution' => $resolution,
        ]);

        $this->recordAuditEvent->execute(
            tenant: $nonConformity->tenant,
            actor: $actor,
            action: 'non_conformity.resolved',
            subjectType: NonConformity::class,
            subjectId: $nonConformity->id,
            reason: $resolution,
            request: $this->request,
        );

        DashboardCache::forget($nonConformity->tenant);

        return $nonConformity;
    }
}


==================== ./app/Domain/Compliance/Actions/RestoreMediaBackupAction.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Compliance\Actions;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

/**
 * The reverse of MirrorMediaBackupAction — copies every object back from
 * the 'backups' disk's media-backup/ prefix onto the 'media' disk,
 * stripping the prefix to restore each file's original path.
 */
class RestoreMediaBackupAction
{
    private const string PREFIX = 'media-backup';

    /**
     * @return int number of files restored
     */
    public function execute(): int
    {
        $count = 0;

        foreach (Storage::disk('backups')->allFiles(self::PREFIX) as $backedUpPath) {
            $originalPath = Str::after($backedUpPath, self::PREFIX.'/');

            Storage::disk('media')->put(
                $originalPath,
                Storage::disk('backups')->get($backedUpPath),
            );
            $count++;
        }

        return $count;
    }
}

 * is deliberately no code path here that would let you.

/**
 * Deliberately NOT BelongsToTenant — a row here can reference two tenants

 * written through the app's normal connection either: this pins its own
 * $connection to `pgsql_admin`, the only connection the migration grants
 * any access to at all (see the migration's own docblock) — a plain
 * `SecurityEvent::create()` from request-serving code works exactly like
 * any other Eloquent model, it's just always talking to the admin

 * Append-only (no update/delete route here, and the DB itself refuses
 * regardless of role — see the migration).

 * @property string|null $subject_id
 * @property string|null $ip
 * @property string|null $user_agent
 * @property string $request_id
 * @property Carbon $occurred_at
 */
class SecurityEvent extends Model
{
    use HasUuidv7;

    protected $connection = 'pgsql_admin';

    public const UPDATED_AT = null;

    public const CREATED_AT = null;

    protected $fillable = [
        'type', 'actor_id', 'actor_label_snapshot', 'tenant_claimed_id', 'tenant_actual_id',
        'route_name', 'method', 'path', 'subject_type', 'subject_id', 'ip', 'user_agent',
        'request_id', 'occurred_at',
    ];

    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'type' => SecurityEventType::class,
            'occurred_at' => 'datetime',
        ];
    }

==================== ./app/Domain/Equipment/Actions/CreateDeviceAction.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Equipment\Actions;

use App\Domain\Compliance\Actions\RecordAuditEventAction;
use App\Domain\Equipment\Models\Device;
use App\Domain\Tenancy\Models\Tenant;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Support\Api\ApiException;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class CreateDeviceAction
{
    public function __construct(
        private RecordAuditEventAction $recordAuditEvent,
        private Request $request,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  array<string, mixed>  $attributes
     */
    public function execute(Tenant $tenant, User $actor, array $attributes): Device
    {
        if (Device::where('serial_number', $attributes['serial_number'])->exists()) {
            throw new ApiException('DEVICE_SERIAL_NUMBER_TAKEN', 'A device with this serial number already exists.', 409);
        }

        $device = Device::create($attributes + ['tenant_id' => $tenant->id]);
        $device->refresh();

        $this->recordAuditEvent->execute(
            tenant: $tenant,
            actor: $actor,
            action: 'device.created',
            subjectType: Device::class,
            subjectId: $device->id,
            newValues: $attributes,
            request: $this->request,
        );

        return $device;
    }
}


==================== ./app/Domain/Equipment/Actions/CreateDeviceProgramAction.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Equipment\Actions;

use App\Domain\Compliance\Actions\RecordAuditEventAction;
use App\Domain\Equipment\Models\Device;
use App\Domain\Equipment\Models\DeviceProgram;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Support\Api\ApiException;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class CreateDeviceProgramAction
{
    public function __construct(
        private RecordAuditEventAction $recordAuditEvent,
        private Request $request,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  array<string, mixed>  $attributes
     */
    public function execute(Device $device, User $actor, array $attributes): DeviceProgram
    {
        if ($device->programs()->where('name', $attributes['name'])->exists()) {
            throw new ApiException('DEVICE_PROGRAM_NAME_TAKEN', 'This device already has a program with this name.', 409);
        }

        $program = $device->programs()->create($attributes + ['tenant_id' => $device->tenant_id]);
        // is_active isn't always in $attributes; the in-memory model won't
        // see its DB-level default unless re-read (same pitfall as Product).
        $program->refresh();

        $this->recordAuditEvent->execute(
            tenant: $device->tenant,
            actor: $actor,
            action: 'device_program.created',
            subjectType: DeviceProgram::class,
            subjectId: $program->id,
            newValues: $attributes,
            request: $this->request,
        );

        return $program;
    }
}

==================== ./app/Domain/Equipment/Actions/UpdateDeviceAction.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Equipment\Actions;

use App\Domain\Compliance\Actions\RecordAuditEventAction;
use App\Domain\Equipment\Models\Device;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Support\Api\ApiException;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class UpdateDeviceAction
{
    public function __construct(
        private RecordAuditEventAction $recordAuditEvent,
        private Request $request,
    ) {}

    /**
     * @param  array<string, mixed>  $attributes
     */
    public function execute(Device $device, User $actor, array $attributes): Device
    {
        if (
            isset($attributes['serial_number'])
            && Device::where('serial_number', $attributes['serial_number'])->where('id', '!=', $device->id)->exists()
        ) {
            throw new ApiException('DEVICE_SERIAL_NUMBER_TAKEN', 'A device with this serial number already exists.', 409);
        }

        $oldValues = $device->only(array_keys($attributes));
        $device->update($attributes);

        $this->recordAuditEvent->execute(
            tenant: $device->tenant,
            actor: $actor,
            action: 'device.updated',
            subjectType: Device::class,
            subjectId: $device->id,
            oldValues: $oldValues,
            newValues: $attributes,
            request: $this->request,
        );

        return $device;
    }
}

==================== ./app/Domain/Equipment/Models/Device.php ====================

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Equipment\Models;

use App\Domain\Equipment\Enums\DeviceKind;
use App\Domain\Equipment\Enums\DeviceStatus;
use App\Domain\Tenancy\Models\Site;
use App\Support\Concerns\BelongsToTenant;
use App\Support\Concerns\HasUuidv7;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\HasMany;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;
use Illuminate\Support\Carbon;

/**
 * @property string $id
 * @property string $tenant_id
 * @property string $site_id
 * @property string $name
 * @property string $serial_number
 * @property DeviceKind $kind
 * @property DeviceStatus $status
 * @property string|null $manufacturer
 * @property string|null $model
 * @property Carbon|null $commissioned_at
 * @property Carbon|null $decommissioned_at
 * @property string|null $notes
 */
class Device extends Model
{
    use BelongsToTenant;
    use HasUuidv7;
    use SoftDeletes;

    protected $fillable = [
        'tenant_id', 'site_id', 'name', 'serial_number', 'kind', 'status',
        'manufacturer', 'model', 'commissioned_at', 'decommissioned_at', 'notes',
    ];

    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'kind' => DeviceKind::class,
            'status' => DeviceStatus::class,
            'commissioned_at' => 'date',
            'decommissioned_at' => 'date',
        ];
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<Site, $this>
     */
    public function site(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Site::class)->withTrashed();
    }

    /**
     * @return HasMany<DeviceProgram, $this>
     */
    public function programs(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(DeviceProgram::class);
    }

    /**
     * @return HasMany<MaintenanceRecord, $this>
     */
    public function maintenanceRecords(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(MaintenanceRecord::class);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Domain\Equipment\Models;

use App\Support\Concerns\HasUuidv7;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\SoftDeletes;

/**
 * @property string $id
 * @property string $tenant_id
 * @property string $device_id
 * @property string $name
 * @property int $target_temperature_celsius
 * @property int $plateau_minutes
 * @property bool $is_active
 */
class DeviceProgram extends Model
{
    use BelongsToTenant;
    use HasUuidv7;
    use SoftDeletes;

    protected $fillable = [
        'tenant_id', 'device_id', 'name', 'target_temperature_celsius', 'plateau_minutes', 'is_active',
    ];

    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'target_temperature_celsius' => 'integer',
            'plateau_minutes' => 'integer',
            'is_active' => 'boolean',
        ];
    }

    /**
     * @return BelongsTo<Device, $this>
     */
    public function device(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(Device::class);
    }
}
