==================== ./CLAUDE.md ====================

You are the lead backend/web engineer on SteriQore, a multi-tenant dental SaaS MVP.
I own the server + web; a second dev builds a separate Flutter app against my API.
Work sprint by sprint. Do NOT scaffold everything at once.

## PRODUCT
Sterilization traceability + inventory for dental practices, modelled on Sterily.fr.
Core loop: receive stock (batch+expiry) -> prepare a load -> run an autoclave cycle
-> record control tests -> an authorized user RELEASES the cycle (compliant/rejected)
-> print one unique 2D-coded label per pouch -> scan at the chair before use
-> link pouch->cycle->device->practitioner->procedure->pseudonymized patient
-> one click produces the inspection-ready evidence dossier PDF.
Also: control-test logbook (vacuum/Bowie-Dick/Helix/biological) with missing-test alerts,
low-stock and near-expiry alerts, full searchable history, 30-day trial.
OUT OF SCOPE: billing, marketplace, complex multi-site, predictive analytics,
universal autoclave compatibility, more than one partner connector.

## STACK — do not substitute, do not add heavy deps without asking
PHP 8.4 | Laravel 13 | Octane + FrankenPHP | Inertia 3 (@inertiajs/react ^3) |
React 19 + TypeScript strict | Vite 7 | Tailwind 4 | shadcn/ui
PostgreSQL 18 (single shared DB + tenant_id + Row-Level Security) | Redis 8 | Horizon
S3-compatible storage (MinIO locally), private buckets, presigned URLs only
Resend for all mail (resend/resend-laravel) | Docker for dev/CI/staging/prod
Web auth = Inertia session. Mobile auth = Sanctum tokens.
Packages: spatie/laravel-multitenancy ^4, spatie/laravel-permission ^6 (teams mode,
team_foreign_key=tenant_id), spatie/laravel-activitylog, spatie/laravel-medialibrary,
spatie/laravel-data, spatie/laravel-query-builder, spatie/laravel-backup,
dedoc/scramble (OpenAPI 3.1), bacon/bacon-qr-code, tecnickcom/tc-lib-barcode (DataMatrix),
spatie/laravel-pdf, maatwebsite/excel, sanctum, horizon, pest ^4, larastan, pint, sentry.
AI (OFF by default, STERIQORE_FEATURE_AI=false): Laravel AI SDK + OpenAI provider.

## NAMING
repo/db/compose/redis-prefix `steriqore`; S3 buckets steriqore-media|exports|backups;
app-specific env vars prefixed STERIQORE_; tenants by subdomain {slug}.steriqore.<tld>;
APP_DOMAIN in env, never hard-coded; mail from "SteriQore <no-reply@...>".

## ARCHITECTURE
app/Domain/<Context>/{Models,Actions,Data,Events,Policies} for Tenancy, Identity,
Catalog, Purchasing, Inventory, Equipment, Sterilization, Labeling, Traceability,
Reporting, Compliance, AI. Controllers validate -> authorize -> delegate to a
single-purpose Action -> respond. No business logic in controllers, models or React.
Http/Controllers/Web (Inertia) and Http/Controllers/Api/V1 (mobile REST) are separate.

## TENANCY (most important decision)
Every tenant-owned table has non-null tenant_id (UUID, FK, indexed); every unique
constraint is scoped (tenant_id, ...). spatie/laravel-multitenancy resolves the current
tenant; a BelongsToTenant trait adds a global scope + auto-fills on create; PostgreSQL
RLS on current_setting('app.tenant_id') is enabled on every tenant table as a second
line of defence. The tenant NEVER comes from a request parameter — only from the
session/token. Any route accepting a client-supplied tenant id is a bug.

## API CONVENTIONS — freeze in S0, they unblock the mobile dev
/api/v1, JSON only, snake_case, ISO-8601 UTC, UUIDv7 ids.
One error shape always:
  {"error":{"code":"CYCLE_NOT_RELEASED","message":"...","details":{},"request_id":"..."}}
Stable machine `code` per business rule; mobile branches on code, never on message.
Status: 200/201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 state conflict, 410 recalled/expired,
422, 429, 5xx. Cursor pagination. ETag on read-heavy resources.
IDEMPOTENCY IS MANDATORY on every mutation: client sends Idempotency-Key; server stores
key + request hash + response in Redis 24h and replays it on repeat.
OpenAPI generated by Scramble, committed to docs/openapi.yaml, covered by contract tests
so it can never silently drift.

## INVARIANTS — enforce in DB *and* code, one test each
1. Stock is DERIVED from an append-only stock_movements ledger. No endpoint sets a
   quantity directly. stock_levels is a projection, rebuildable by replay.
2. No label may exist for a cycle that is not released+compliant.
3. A cycle_release row is immutable. Mistakes are corrected by a non_conformity +
   recall, never by UPDATE.
4. A reprint requires a reason, increments print_counter, writes a label_prints row.
5. Scanning a recalled/expired label returns 410 with a blocking code + audit event.
6. Users are soft-disabled, never deleted; past evidence keeps their identity.
7. Evidence tables (cycles, releases, labels, usages, movements, audit_events) have
   NO delete route, and a PostgreSQL trigger raises on UPDATE/DELETE of audit_events.

## LABELS
One label per pouch. Printed: sterilizer id, cycle/load number, sterilization date+time,
use-by date (DLU), operator, sequence in cycle, practice/site. Support QR AND DataMatrix
(French readers expect DataMatrix). The 2D payload is opaque: urn:steriqore:label:<uuid>
or a short URL containing only the label UUID — never patient data, never a secret.
DLU comes from a per-tenant rule table (packaging x storage, EN 868 defaults) and is
frozen onto the label at print time so later rule changes never rewrite past evidence.

## CROSS-CUTTING
Append-only audit_events (actor, tenant, action, subject, old/new values, reason, ip,
request_id). Server-side Policies on every route + an IDOR suite that walks every
resource as a foreign tenant expecting 403/404. Transactions with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
on stock rows. External API outage must never break the core product. Common screens
< 2s; evidence search < 2s at pilot volume (index deliberately, GIN/tsvector).
Patient data is pseudonymous only; NO real patient data until a written GDPR/HDS
decision exists. Demo/pilot datasets fully synthetic.

## AI RULES (when enabled later)
Suggest-only: autoclave ticket OCR, delivery-note extraction, natural-language search
(emits a constrained filter DTO — never SQL, never raw data), alert digests.
A human confirms before any write; values are source=ai_suggested until confirmed.
No AI output is ever stored as evidence. No patient identifier ever leaves in a prompt.
Every journey must work fully with AI switched off.

## BUILD ORDER — one item at a time, do not start the next until the current is green
S0  repo+skeleton | PostgreSQL multi-tenant model + ERD | OpenAPI v1 + error conventions
    (HIGHEST PRIORITY, it unblocks the mobile dev) | Docker Compose (PG18, Redis 8, MinIO)
S1  tenants/sites/rooms/locations + RLS | identity: invitations, sessions, Sanctum,
    reset, revocation | RBAC teams mode (owner, admin, stock_manager, releaser,
    practitioner, viewer) + Policies + IDOR suite | append-only audit log
S2  catalogue | suppliers | purchase orders + partial receipts | inventory engine
    (batches, expiries, movement ledger, locations, counts) | alert engine
S3  devices/programs/maintenance | cycles + loads + control tests + attachments +
    state machine | release service (immutable) | label service (QR+DataMatrix, DLU,
    PDF sheets, justified reprints) | scan resolution endpoint
S4  pseudonymized patient ids | traceability chain label->procedure->practitioner |
    multi-criteria search <2s | evidence dossier PDF + CSV/XLSX exports |
    non-conformities: recall, quarantine, audited corrections
S5  security campaign | staging + logs + monitoring | backups WITH a proven restore |
    performance at pilot volume | documentation a third party can install from
S6  fix critical/high defects | production deploy + tested rollback | full data+file
    portability export

## STATE MACHINES
purchase_order: draft -> ordered -> partially_received -> received -> closed | cancelled
cycle: draft -> running -> completed -> awaiting_release -> released | rejected (terminal)
label: created -> printed -> used | expired | recalled | voided

## ACCEPTANCE — automated test for each, a red critical blocks release
REC-01 user of practice A requests a resource of practice B -> refusal + no leak + log
REC-02 same receipt submitted twice -> exactly one stock movement
REC-03 label generation for a rejected cycle -> explicit block
REC-05 reprint -> reason, counter, audit
REC-06 disabled user -> past evidence keeps their identity
REC-07 partner API outage -> core product still usable
REC-09 search by patient/cycle/batch -> complete result < 2s at pilot volume
REC-10 restore PG + S3 backup -> data and attachments fully recovered

## HOW TO WORK
One backlog item per PR, branch feat/S3-ANA-04-labels, conventional commits.
Every feature ships with tests; untested = not done.
Never invent a business rule: implement the safe default, mark // DECISION NEEDED:
and append it to docs/open-questions.md.
After each item report: what you built, migrations, tests, OpenAPI delta, open decisions.

S7 (post app-shell UI build-out) works off docs/ui-backlog.md — the full UI-01..UI-31
queue, its per-task contract, and design constraints. Read it before starting any
UI-XX item; update its Status column as part of that item's commit.

START NOW with S0: propose the repo structure and the full ERD (tenants, sites, rooms,
locations, users, roles, audit) as docs/erd.md, ask me anything blocking, and wait for
my approval before writing migrations.

<?php

use Spatie\Backup\Notifications\Notifiable;
use Spatie\Backup\Notifications\Notifications\BackupHasFailedNotification;

return [

    'backup' => [
        /*
         * The name of this application. You can use this name to monitor
         * the backups.
         */
        'name' => env('APP_NAME', 'laravel-backup'),

        'source' => [
            'files' => [
                /*
                 * Empty on purpose: the codebase lives in git, and every
                 * user-generated file (cycle attachments, etc.) lives on
                 * the 'media' S3 disk, not local storage — zipping
                 * base_path() would just duplicate the repo into every
                 * backup. See App\Domain\Compliance\Actions
                 * \MirrorMediaBackupAction for how the S3 side is backed
                 * up instead (REC-10: "restore PG + S3 backup").
                 */
                'include' => [],

                /*
                 * These directories and files will be excluded from the backup.
                 *
                 * Directories used by the backup process will automatically be excluded.
                 */
                'exclude' => [
                    base_path('vendor'),
                    base_path('node_modules'),
                    storage_path('framework'),
                ],

                /*
                 * Determines if symlinks should be followed.
                 */
                'follow_links' => false,

                /*
                 * Determines if it should avoid unreadable folders.
                 */
                'ignore_unreadable_directories' => false,

                /*
                 * This path is used to make directories in resulting zip-file relative
                 * Set to `null` to include complete absolute path
                 * Example: base_path()
                 */
                'relative_path' => null,
            ],

            /*
             * The names of the connections to the databases that should be backed up
             * MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite and Mongo databases are supported.
             *
             * The content of the database dump may be customized for each connection
             * by adding a 'dump' key to the connection settings in config/database.php.
             * E.g.
             * 'mysql' => [
             *       ...
             *      'dump' => [
             *           'exclude_tables' => [
             *                'table_to_exclude_from_backup',
             *                'another_table_to_exclude'
             *            ]
             *       ],
             * ],
             *
             * If you are using only InnoDB tables on a MySQL server, you can
             * also supply the useSingleTransaction option to avoid table locking.
             *
             * E.g.
             * 'mysql' => [
             *       ...
             *      'dump' => [
             *           'useSingleTransaction' => true,
             *       ],
             * ],
             *
             * For a complete list of available customization options, see https://github.com/spatie/db-dumper
             */
            /*
             * pgsql_admin, not pgsql: the default connection runs as
             * steriqore_app, a restricted role with RLS enforced and no
             * BYPASSRLS — a full-database pg_dump (no app.tenant_id
             * session var, no tenant to scope to) fails outright against
             * a table with RLS enabled from that role. pgsql_admin is the
             * elevated 'steriqore' role already used for migrations.
             */
            'databases' => [
                'pgsql_admin',
            ],
        ],

        /*
         * The database dump can be compressed to decrease disk space usage.
         *
         * Out of the box Laravel-backup supplies
         * Spatie\DbDumper\Compressors\GzipCompressor::class.
         *
         * You can also create custom compressor. More info on that here:
         * https://github.com/spatie/db-dumper#using-compression
         *
         * If you do not want any compressor at all, set it to null.
         */
        'database_dump_compressor' => null,

        /*
         * If specified, the database dumped file name will contain a timestamp (e.g.: 'Y-m-d-H-i-s').
         */
        'database_dump_file_timestamp_format' => null,

        /*
         * The base of the dump filename, either 'database' or 'connection'
         *
         * If 'database' (default), the dumped filename will contain the database name.
         * If 'connection', the dumped filename will contain the connection name.
         */
        'database_dump_filename_base' => 'database',

        /*
         * The file extension used for the database dump files.
         *
         * If not specified, the file extension will be .archive for MongoDB and .sql for all other databases
         * The file extension should be specified without a leading .

        'database_dump_file_extension' => '',

             * ZipArchive::CM_BZIP2

             * The compression level corresponding to the used algorithm; an integer between 0 and 9.
             *
             * Check supported levels for the chosen algorithm, usually 1 means the fastest and weakest compression,
             * while 9 the slowest and strongest one.

     *

     * the `Spatie\Backup\Notifications\Notifications` classes.

    'notifications' => [
        'notifications' => [
            BackupHasFailedNotification::class => ['mail'],
            UnhealthyBackupWasFoundNotification::class => ['mail'],
            CleanupHasFailedNotification::class => ['mail'],
            BackupWasSuccessfulNotification::class => ['mail'],

        |
        */
        'remote_disk' => null,
        'remote_prefix' => null,

        /*
        |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
        | Force Resync
        |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
        |
        | When dealing with a multi server setup as above, it's possible
        | for the clean up that occurs after entire queue has been run to only
        | cleanup the server that the last AfterImportJob runs on. The rest of the server
        | would still have the local temporary file stored on it. In this case your
        | local storage limits can be exceeded and future imports won't be processed.
        | To mitigate this you can set this config value to be true, so that after every
        | queued chunk is processed the local temporary file is deleted on the server that
        | processed it.
        |
        */
        'force_resync_remote' => null,
    ],
];

<?php

use App\Domain\Tenancy\Models\Tenant;

    /*
     * No tenant_finder: we don't resolve the tenant from the domain/subdomain
     * or a request parameter. The tenant comes from the Sanctum token (API)
     * or the web session (Inertia) only — see App\Http\Middleware\Api\SetCurrentTenant.
     * Any tenant-finder that reads a client-supplied value would violate the
     * tenancy invariant in CLAUDE.md.

    'tenant_finder' => null,

     */
    'tenant_artisan_search_fields' => [
        'id',
    ],

     * Deliberately empty: SteriQore is single shared database + tenant_id +
     * RLS (CLAUDE.md), not one database per tenant, so none of the built-in
     * switch tasks (PrefixCacheTask, SwitchTenantDatabaseTask, ...) apply.
     * Setting the Postgres RLS session variable is handled by our own
     * App\Http\Middleware\Api\SetCurrentTenant instead, wrapping the request
     * in a transaction (SET LOCAL only lasts for the current transaction).
     */
    'switch_tenant_tasks' => [],

    /*
     * Our own tenant model — implements IsTenant directly rather than
     * extending Spatie\Multitenancy\Models\Tenant, since that base class

     */
    'tenant_model' => Tenant::class,

    /*
     * If there is a current tenant when dispatching a job, the id of the current tenant

     * tenant on the job will be made current.
     */
    'queues_are_tenant_aware_by_default' => true,

    /*

     */
    'tenant_database_connection_name' => null,

    /*
     * The connection name to reach the landlord database.
     */
    'landlord_database_connection_name' => null,

    /*
     * This key will be used to associate the current tenant in the context
     */
    'current_tenant_context_key' => 'tenantId',

    /*
     * This key will be used to bind the current tenant in the container.
     */
    'current_tenant_container_key' => 'currentTenant',

    /*
     * Set it to `true` if you like to cache the tenant(s) routes
     * in a shared file using the `SwitchRouteCacheTask`.
     */
    'shared_routes_cache' => false,

    /*

    'actions' => [

<?php

use Illuminate\Support\Str;

return [

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Default Session Driver
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This option determines the default session driver that is utilized for
    | incoming requests. Laravel supports a variety of storage options to
    | persist session data. Database storage is a great default choice.
    |
    | Supported: "file", "cookie", "database", "memcached",
    |            "redis", "dynamodb", "array"
    |
    */

    'driver' => env('SESSION_DRIVER', 'database'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Lifetime
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Here you may specify the number of minutes that you wish the session
    | to be allowed to remain idle before it expires. If you want them
    | to expire immediately when the browser is closed then you may
    | indicate that via the expire_on_close configuration option.
    |
    */

    'lifetime' => (int) env('SESSION_LIFETIME', 120),

    'expire_on_close' => env('SESSION_EXPIRE_ON_CLOSE', false),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Encryption
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This option allows you to easily specify that all of your session data
    | should be encrypted before it's stored. All encryption is performed
    | automatically by Laravel and you may use the session like normal.
    |
    */

    'encrypt' => env('SESSION_ENCRYPT', false),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session File Location
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | When utilizing the "file" session driver, the session files are placed
    | on disk. The default storage location is defined here; however, you
    | are free to provide another location where they should be stored.
    |
    */

    'files' => storage_path('framework/sessions'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Database Connection
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | When using the "database" or "redis" session drivers, you may specify a
    | connection that should be used to manage these sessions. This should
    | correspond to a connection in your database configuration options.
    |
    */

    'connection' => env('SESSION_CONNECTION'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Database Table
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | When using the "database" session driver, you may specify the table to
    | be used to store sessions. Of course, a sensible default is defined
    | for you; however, you're welcome to change this to another table.
    |
    */

    'table' => env('SESSION_TABLE', 'sessions'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Cache Store
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | When using one of the framework's cache driven session backends, you may
    | define the cache store which should be used to store the session data
    | between requests. This must match one of your defined cache stores.
    |
    | Affects: "dynamodb", "memcached", "redis"
    |
    */

    'store' => env('SESSION_STORE'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Sweeping Lottery
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Some session drivers must manually sweep their storage location to get
    | rid of old sessions from storage. Here are the chances that it will
    | happen on a given request. By default, the odds are 2 out of 100.
    |
    */

    'lottery' => [2, 100],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Cookie Name
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Here you may change the name of the session cookie that is created by
    | the framework. Typically, you should not need to change this value
    | since doing so does not grant a meaningful security improvement.
    |
    */

    'cookie' => env(

        Str::slug((string) env('APP_NAME', 'laravel')).'-session',
    ),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Cookie Path
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------

    | be regarded as available. Typically, this will be the root path of
    | your application, but you're free to change this when necessary.
    |
    */

    'path' => env('SESSION_PATH', '/'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Session Cookie Domain
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | This value determines the domain and subdomains the session cookie is
    | available to. By default, the cookie will be available to the root
    | domain without subdomains. Typically, this shouldn't be changed.
    |
    */

    'domain' => env('SESSION_DOMAIN'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | HTTPS Only Cookies
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | By setting this option to true, session cookies will only be sent back
    | to the server if the browser has a HTTPS connection. This will keep
    | the cookie from being sent to you when it can't be done securely.
    |
    */

    'secure' => env('SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | HTTP Access Only
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Setting this value to true will prevent JavaScript from accessing the
    | value of the cookie and the cookie will only be accessible through
    | the HTTP protocol. It's unlikely you should disable this option.
    |

    'http_only' => env('SESSION_HTTP_ONLY', true),

    /*

    | Same-Site Cookies
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------

    | This option determines how your cookies behave when cross-site requests
    | take place, and can be used to mitigate CSRF attacks. By default, we
    | will set this value to "lax" to permit secure cross-site requests.
    |
    | See: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie#samesitesamesite-value
    |
    | Supported: "lax", "strict", "none", null

    'same_site' => env('SESSION_SAME_SITE', 'lax'),

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Partitioned Cookies
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    |
    | Setting this value to true will tie the cookie to the top-level site for

    | when flagged "secure" and the Same-Site attribute is set to "none".
    |
    */

    'partitioned' => env('SESSION_PARTITIONED_COOKIE', false),

    /*

    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------

==================== ./database/factories/UserFactory.php ====================

<?php

namespace Database\Factories;

use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\Factory;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

/**
 * @extends Factory<User>
 */
class UserFactory extends Factory
{
    /**
     * The current password being used by the factory.
     */
    protected static ?string $password;

    /**
     * Define the model's default state.
     *
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     */
    public function definition(): array
    {
        return [
            'name' => fake()->name(),
            'email' => fake()->unique()->safeEmail(),
            'email_verified_at' => now(),
            'password' => static::$password ??= Hash::make('password'),
            'remember_token' => Str::random(10),
            'two_factor_secret' => null,
            'two_factor_recovery_codes' => null,
            'two_factor_confirmed_at' => null,
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Indicate that the model's email address should be unverified.
     */
    public function unverified(): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn (array $attributes) => [
            'email_verified_at' => null,
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * Indicate that the model has two-factor authentication configured.
     */
    public function withTwoFactor(): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn (array $attributes) => [
            'two_factor_secret' => encrypt('secret'),
            'two_factor_recovery_codes' => encrypt(json_encode(['recovery-code-1'])),
            'two_factor_confirmed_at' => now(),
        ]);
    }
}

==================== ./database/migrations/2026_07_25_000001_add_row_level_security_to_tenant_tables.php ====================

<?php

use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

/**
 * The second line of defence behind the ORM's TenantScope (see
 * App\Support\Tenancy\TenantScope): even a forgotten scope, a raw query, or
 * a bug can't leak across tenants, because Postgres itself refuses the row.
 *
 * Scope note: this covers sites/rooms/storage_locations only — the tables
 * S1-ANA-01 owns. tenant_user, invitations, and personal_access_tokens carry
 * a tenant_id too but are *resolved during* authentication (you must read a
 * tenant_user row to find out which tenant a login belongs to, before any
 * "current tenant" exists to scope by) — RLS on those needs a policy shaped
 * around that bootstrap lookup, which is S1-ANA-02's job when the
 * invitation/session flows are actually built, not guessed at here.
 *
 * FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY matters: without it, the table owner (the
 * elevated migrations role) bypasses RLS by default, silently defeating it.
 * The running application must connect as a different, non-superuser,
 * non-owner role for any of this to actually apply — see
 * docker/postgres/init/01-create-app-role.sql and config/database.php.
 */
return new class extends Migration
{
    private const TENANT_TABLES = ['sites', 'rooms', 'storage_locations'];

    public function up(): void
    {
        foreach (self::TENANT_TABLES as $table) {
            DB::statement("ALTER TABLE {$table} ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY");
            DB::statement("ALTER TABLE {$table} FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY");

            DB::statement(<<<SQL
                CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON {$table}
                    USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)::uuid)
                    WITH CHECK (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)::uuid)
                SQL);
        }
    }

    public function down(): void
    {
        foreach (self::TENANT_TABLES as $table) {
            DB::statement("DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_isolation ON {$table}");
            DB::statement("ALTER TABLE {$table} NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY");
            DB::statement("ALTER TABLE {$table} DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY");
        }
    }
};

==================== ./database/migrations/2026_07_25_150000_create_audit_events_table.php ====================

<?php

use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;

/**
 * Append-only, twice over: no UPDATE/DELETE route in the app (invariant #7,
 * CLAUDE.md), and — because that alone only stops the app, not a bug or a
 * direct psql session — a trigger that raises on any UPDATE/DELETE
 * regardless of who's connected, including a superuser. RLS (below) is
 * bypassed by superusers/table owners; this trigger is not.
 */
return new class extends Migration
{
    public function up(): void
    {
        Schema::create('audit_events', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->uuid('id')->primary()->default(DB::raw('uuidv7()'));
            $table->foreignUuid('tenant_id')->nullable()->constrained()->cascadeOnDelete();
            $table->foreignUuid('actor_id')->nullable()->constrained('users')->nullOnDelete();
            $table->string('actor_label_snapshot')->nullable();
            $table->string('action');
            $table->string('subject_type');
            $table->uuid('subject_id');
            $table->jsonb('old_values')->nullable();
            $table->jsonb('new_values')->nullable();
            $table->text('reason')->nullable();
            $table->ipAddress('ip')->nullable();
            $table->text('user_agent')->nullable();
            $table->uuid('request_id');
            $table->timestampTz('occurred_at');

            $table->index(['tenant_id', 'occurred_at']);
            $table->index(['subject_type', 'subject_id']);
        });

        // OR REPLACE: `migrate:fresh`/db:wipe drops tables via CASCADE but
        // leaves standalone functions behind, so a plain CREATE FUNCTION
        // fails as "already exists" on the second fresh migration in the
        // same database.
        DB::statement(<<<'SQL'
            CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION prevent_audit_events_modification() RETURNS trigger AS $$
            BEGIN
                RAISE EXCEPTION 'audit_events is append-only: % is not permitted', TG_OP;
            END;
            $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql
            SQL);

        DB::statement(<<<'SQL'
            CREATE TRIGGER audit_events_no_update_delete
                BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON audit_events
                FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION prevent_audit_events_modification()
            SQL);

        // SELECT-only policy, deliberately: some audit events are written
        // during bootstrap flows (login, registration, invitation accept)
        // that run before the `tenant` middleware has set app.tenant_id —
        // there's no "current tenant" transaction to check an insert
        // against yet. Writes are trusted the same way every other
        // Eloquent create() in the app is (only RecordAuditEventAction
        // calls this, never raw client input); reads — the actual leak risk,
        // one practice seeing another's audit trail — are enforced here.
        DB::statement('ALTER TABLE audit_events ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY');
        DB::statement('ALTER TABLE audit_events FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY');
        DB::statement(<<<'SQL'
            CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON audit_events
                FOR SELECT
                USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)::uuid)
            SQL);

        // Without this, RLS-with-no-applicable-policy means "deny all" for
        // INSERT too (not "allow all") — this makes that explicit rather
        // than accidentally relying on the absence of a restriction.
        DB::statement(<<<'SQL'
            CREATE POLICY allow_insert ON audit_events
                FOR INSERT
                WITH CHECK (true)
            SQL);
    }

    public function down(): void
    {
        DB::statement('DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS audit_events_no_update_delete ON audit_events');
        DB::statement('DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS prevent_audit_events_modification()');
        Schema::dropIfExists('audit_events');
    }
};

==================== ./database/migrations/2026_07_27_100001_create_stock_movements_table.php ====================

<?php

use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;

/**
 * The append-only ledger stock is derived from (CLAUDE.md invariant #1):
 * no endpoint sets a quantity directly, stock_levels is a projection built
 * by summing this table, rebuildable by replay
 * (App\Domain\Inventory\Actions\RebuildStockLevelsAction).
 *
 * `qty` is signed: positive credits a location, negative debits it. A
 * transfer is two linked rows (one negative at the source, one positive at
 * the destination) sharing `group_id` — there's no single row that "moves"
 * stock between two locations, only debits and credits, so stock_levels
 * stays a pure SUM(qty) per (batch_id, location_id) regardless of movement
 * type.
 *
 * Append-only twice over, like audit_events: no update/delete route, and a
 * DB trigger that refuses UPDATE/DELETE regardless of role.
 */
return new class extends Migration
{
    public function up(): void
    {
        Schema::create('stock_movements', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->uuid('id')->primary()->default(DB::raw('uuidv7()'));
            $table->foreignUuid('tenant_id')->constrained()->cascadeOnDelete();
            $table->string('type');
            $table->foreignUuid('batch_id')->constrained()->cascadeOnDelete();
            $table->foreignUuid('location_id')->constrained('storage_locations')->cascadeOnDelete();
            $table->integer('qty');
            $table->uuid('group_id')->nullable();
            $table->text('reason')->nullable();
            $table->foreignUuid('actor_id')->nullable()->constrained('users')->nullOnDelete();
            $table->uuid('idempotency_key')->nullable();
            $table->timestampTz('occurred_at');
            $table->timestampTz('created_at');

            $table->index(['tenant_id', 'batch_id', 'location_id']);
            $table->index(['tenant_id', 'group_id']);
            $table->unique(['tenant_id', 'idempotency_key']);
        });

        // Generic (unlike prevent_audit_events_modification, whose message
        // hardcodes that table's name) — reused by every other append-only
        // evidence table from here on.
        DB::statement(<<<'SQL'
            CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION prevent_append_only_table_modification() RETURNS trigger AS $$
            BEGIN
                RAISE EXCEPTION '% is append-only: % is not permitted', TG_TABLE_NAME, TG_OP;
            END;
            $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql
            SQL);

        DB::statement(<<<'SQL'
            CREATE TRIGGER stock_movements_no_update_delete
                BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON stock_movements
                FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION prevent_append_only_table_modification()
            SQL);

        DB::statement('ALTER TABLE stock_movements ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY');
        DB::statement('ALTER TABLE stock_movements FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY');
        DB::statement(<<<'SQL'
            CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON stock_movements
                FOR SELECT
                USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)::uuid)
            SQL);
        DB::statement(<<<'SQL'
            CREATE POLICY allow_insert ON stock_movements
                FOR INSERT
                WITH CHECK (true)
            SQL);
    }

    public function down(): void
    {
        DB::statement('DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS stock_movements_no_update_delete ON stock_movements');
        Schema::dropIfExists('stock_movements');
    }
};

            DB::statement("ALTER TABLE {$table} FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY");
            DB::statement("DROP POLICY IF EXISTS tenant_isolation ON {$table}");

==================== ./database/migrations/2026_08_09_000001_create_security_events_table.php ====================

<?php

use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;

/**
 * A dedicated, operator-only security channel — deliberately NOT
 * audit_events. audit_events is the tenant-visible evidence trail (RLS
 * lets a practice read its OWN rows); a cross-tenant probe, an
 * authorization failure, or an RLS policy rejection belongs to neither the
 * practice that was probed nor the one that did the probing — it's a
 * platform-security signal, only ever meaningful in aggregate/rate-spike
 * form to whoever operates the platform. So: no tenant_id column that
 * "owns" the row (a single row can legitimately reference TWO tenants —
 * claimed and actual — which doesn't fit the BelongsToTenant model at
 * all), RLS enabled with NO permissive policy for the app's own
 * `steriqore_app` role (default-deny, both read and write), and every
 * access — from RecordSecurityEventAction's writes onward — goes through
 * the `pgsql_admin` connection instead (App\Domain\Compliance\Models\
 * SecurityEvent pins its own $connection), the same RLS-bypassing
 * connection SeedPilotVolume/GenerateDataExportJob already use for
 * legitimate cross-tenant admin access. That also sidesteps a subtler
 * problem: an RLS policy rejection means the app's own connection/
 * transaction is already aborted by Postgres at the moment we need to
 * record it — writing through a wholly separate connection is the only
 * way that write can succeed at all.
 *
 * Append-only like every other evidence/security table in this app: no
 * update/delete route, and the DB itself refuses regardless of role.
 */
return new class extends Migration
{
    public function up(): void
    {
        Schema::create('security_events', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->uuid('id')->primary()->default(DB::raw('uuidv7()'));
            $table->string('type');
            $table->uuid('actor_id')->nullable();
            $table->string('actor_label_snapshot')->nullable();
            $table->uuid('tenant_claimed_id')->nullable();
            $table->uuid('tenant_actual_id')->nullable();
            $table->string('route_name')->nullable();
            $table->string('method');
            $table->string('path');
            $table->string('subject_type')->nullable();
            $table->string('subject_id')->nullable();
            $table->ipAddress('ip')->nullable();
            $table->text('user_agent')->nullable();
            $table->uuid('request_id');
            $table->timestampTz('occurred_at');

            // No FKs: actor/tenant ids here are read back from a live
            // request (or, for tenant_actual_id, a cross-tenant lookup) —
            // this table must never fail to record an event because a
            // referenced row got cleaned up, and a garbage/spoofed id in
            // a probe attempt is exactly the kind of thing worth keeping
            // even if it doesn't resolve to anything real.
            $table->index(['type', 'occurred_at']);
            $table->index(['tenant_claimed_id', 'occurred_at']);
            $table->index('actor_id');
        });

        DB::statement(<<<'SQL'
            CREATE TRIGGER security_events_no_update_delete
                BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON security_events
                FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION prevent_append_only_table_modification()
            SQL);

        // No policies at all, deliberately: RLS-with-no-applicable-policy
        // is default-deny for every command, for every role subject to it.
        // The `steriqore_app` role (what every tenant-facing request runs
        // as) is subject to RLS and has no policy here, so it can neither
        // read nor write this table under any circumstance — only the
        // `pgsql_admin` connection (bypasses RLS entirely, see class docblock)
        // can, and only App\Domain\Compliance\Models\SecurityEvent uses it.
        DB::statement('ALTER TABLE security_events ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY');
        DB::statement('ALTER TABLE security_events FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY');
    }

    public function down(): void
    {
        DB::statement('DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS security_events_no_update_delete ON security_events');
        Schema::dropIfExists('security_events');
    }
};


==================== ./database/seeders/DatabaseSeeder.php ====================

<?php

namespace Database\Seeders;

use App\Domain\Identity\Actions\RegisterTenantAction;
use App\Domain\Tenancy\Models\Tenant;
use App\Support\Tenancy\TenantContext;
use Illuminate\Database\Console\Seeds\WithoutModelEvents;
use Illuminate\Database\Seeder;

class DatabaseSeeder extends Seeder
{
    use WithoutModelEvents;

    /**
     * A bare `User::create()` (the Laravel starter-kit default) has no
     * tenant membership at all, so it can't get past Web\SetCurrentTenant
     * on any real page (S7) — going through the same
     * RegisterTenantAction the "create a practice" flow actually uses
     * means this seeded account is a real owner of a real practice, not
     * a login that only satisfies auth but nothing downstream of it.
     */
    public function run(): void
    {
        if (Tenant::where('slug', 'demo')->exists()) {
            return;
        }

        $result = app(RegisterTenantAction::class)->execute(
            tenantName: 'Demo Practice',
            tenantSlug: 'demo',
            ownerName: 'Admin',
            ownerEmail: 'admin@steriqore.local',
            password: 'password',
        );

        TenantContext::run($result['tenant'], function () use ($result) {
            $result['tenant']->sites()->create(['name' => 'Cabinet Principal']);
        });
    }
}


==================== ./docker/postgres/init/01-create-app-role.sql ====================

-- Row-Level Security only works as a real second line of defence if the
-- role the running application connects as is NOT a superuser and does NOT
-- own the tables: Postgres superusers and table owners bypass RLS entirely,
-- regardless of ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The POSTGRES_USER created by
-- the official postgres image (here: "steriqore") owns the whole cluster, so it
-- must be reserved for migrations/admin tasks only. The app connects as this
-- restricted role instead. See docs/erd.md section 4 and CLAUDE.md's
-- tenancy invariant.
DO
$$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'steriqore_app') THEN
        CREATE ROLE steriqore_app LOGIN PASSWORD 'steriqore_app_secret' NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE;
    END IF;
END
$$;

GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE steriqore TO steriqore_app;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO steriqore_app;

-- Tables/sequences created later by migrations (run as the superuser) won't
-- automatically grant to steriqore_app — ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES covers
-- every table the superuser creates from here on.
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE steriqore IN SCHEMA public
    GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO steriqore_app;
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE steriqore IN SCHEMA public
    GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO steriqore_app;

-- Also grant on whatever already exists at init time (harmless if empty).
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO steriqore_app;
GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public TO steriqore_app;

# =============================================================================
# SteriQore — Staging Docker Compose (S5-ANA-02)

# A skeleton, not a deployed environment: no staging host, domain, Sentry
# project, or mail/S3 account exists yet (see docs/open-questions.md,

#   - TLS/reverse proxy and the public domain — FrankenPHP serves plain
#     HTTP on :8000 (see docker/supervisord.conf); something in front of
#     this stack has to terminate TLS and forward to it.
#   - Whether Postgres/Redis/S3 stay self-hosted (as below, mirroring
#     local dev) or move to managed services later.

# Copy .env.staging.example to .env.staging and fill in every CHANGE_ME
# before using this file. Bring up with:
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml --env-file .env.staging up -d

        condition: service_healthy

      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 15s

    image: postgres:18-alpine
    container_name: steriqore-postgres-staging

    # app container on the internal network. Use an SSH tunnel for direct
    # access if it's ever genuinely needed.

      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

    image: redis:8-alpine

    volumes:
      - redis-data-staging:/data

      - steriqore-staging

  minio-init:

# All services use non-conflicting external ports to avoid clashes with
# locally running services (including the steriqore stack). Internal ports remain
# standard for inter-container communication via the shared 'steriqore' network.
#
# Port Mapping Reference:
#   PostgreSQL:     5455  → 5432
#   Redis:          6395  → 6379
#   Mailpit SMTP:   1055  → 1025
#   Mailpit Web:    8035  → 8025
#   MinIO API:      9023  → 9000
#   MinIO Console:  9024  → 9001
#   Steriqore App:  8010  → 8000

services:
  # ─── Steriqore Application ──────────────────────────────────────────
  app:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile

      - '8010:8000'

      watch:

          target: /app/bootstrap
        - action: sync+restart
          path: ./config
          target: /app/config

            - public/hot

        - action: sync+restart
          path: ./.env
          target: /app/.env
        # Dependency / image changes: full rebuild
        - action: rebuild
          path: ./composer.lock
        - action: rebuild
          path: ./composer.json

      - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=minioadmin

==================== ./docs/00-BUILD-BRIEF.md ====================

# BUILD PROMPT — **SteriQore**
### Dental Sterilization Traceability & Inventory SaaS (MVP)

> Paste this whole document as the opening prompt of a Claude Code / agent session at the root of an empty repo.
> It is written to be executed sprint by sprint, not all at once. Sections 1–8 are permanent context; section 9 is the work order.

---

## 0. YOUR ROLE

You are the lead backend/web engineer on a two-developer HealthTech MVP. You own **everything server-side and web**: architecture, PostgreSQL schema, Laravel backend, the REST API consumed by a separate Flutter mobile app, the React/Inertia admin web app, Docker, CI/CD, security and documentation.

You do **not** own the Flutter app. A second developer builds it against your API. Therefore: **the OpenAPI contract is a first-class deliverable, versioned and frozen before implementation**, and any breaking change to it is a decision, not a commit.

Working rules:

- Never invent business rules. If a rule is ambiguous, implement the safest behaviour, mark it `// DECISION NEEDED:` and list it in `docs/open-questions.md`.
- Never write code that lets evidence be silently deleted or overwritten. This is a regulated-adjacent product; auditability beats convenience every single time.
- Every feature ships with tests. A feature with no test is not done.
- Small, reviewable PRs, one per backlog item, branch `feat/S3-ANA-04-labels`, conventional commits.

## 1. THE PRODUCT

**Name: SteriQore.** Use it consistently everywhere — repo, package namespace, app name, emails, PDF headers, label footers, API user-agent and error `request_id` prefix. Naming conventions to apply from the first commit:

| Thing | Value |
|---|---|
| Product name | `SteriQore` |
| Repo | `steriqore` (backend/web), `steriqore-mobile` (Flutter, Meryem) |
| PHP namespace | `App\` (Laravel default) with domain contexts under `App\Domain\…`; any published package uses `SteriQore\` |
| DB name / user | `steriqore` |
| Docker compose project | `steriqore` |
| Queue / cache / Redis prefix | `steriqore:` (tenant-scoped keys become `steriqore:t:{tenant_id}:…`) |
| S3 buckets | `steriqore-media`, `steriqore-exports`, `steriqore-backups` |
| Env prefix for app-specific vars | `STERIQORE_` (e.g. `STERIQORE_FEATURE_AI`, `STERIQORE_LABEL_BASE_URL`) |
| Web app URL | `https://app.steriqore.<tld>` — tenants resolved by subdomain `https://{tenant-slug}.steriqore.<tld>` |
| API base | `https://api.steriqore.<tld>/api/v1` (or `/api/v1` on the app host — decide in S0 and freeze it in the OpenAPI contract) |
| Label short-link host | `https://s7q.link/l/{uuid}` or `https://steriqore.<tld>/l/{uuid}` — short host preferred, 2D codes scan faster |
| Sender identity (Resend) | `SteriQore <no-reply@steriqore.<tld>>`, DKIM/SPF/DMARC configured before S1 invitations go out |
| Label / dossier PDF footer | `Generated by SteriQore · {tenant} · {timestamp} · dossier {uuid}` |

The TLD is not decided yet — put it in `.env` as `APP_DOMAIN`, never hard-code it, and flag it in `docs/open-questions.md`.

A multi-tenant SaaS for dental practices, modelled on **Sterily.fr** and its French competitors (e-stericode, SterileConnect), extended with the stock/purchasing module those tools lack.

**The problem it replaces:** practices currently log sterilization in paper notebooks and Excel sheets. When a health authority inspects (ARS in France), they must be able to prove, for a given patient and a given procedure, that the instruments used came out of a *compliant, released* sterilization cycle — with operator, sterilizer, cycle number, date/time, load composition and use-by date.

**The core loop the product must make effortless:**

```
receive stock (batch + expiry)
   → prepare a load and run a sterilization cycle on an autoclave
   → record the cycle result and the control tests
   → an authorized person RELEASES the cycle (compliant / rejected)
   → the system prints one unique 2D-coded label per pouch
   → at the chair, the label is scanned before use
   → the scan links pouch → cycle → device → practitioner → procedure → (pseudonymized) patient
   → one click produces the complete inspection-ready evidence dossier (PDF)
```

**Feature parity targets taken from Sterily:** real-time cycle and test logging; a compliant control-test logbook (vacuum/Bowie-Dick/Helix) with reminder alerts so a mandatory test is never missed; unique QR-coded label per pouch; scan-at-use writing straight into the patient record; complete searchable history; one-click inspection dossier; 15–30 day self-serve trial.

**Deliberately out of MVP scope** (do not build, do not scaffold): advanced SaaS billing, marketplace, complex multi-site, predictive analytics, universal autoclave compatibility, heavy per-tenant customization, more than one real partner connector.

## 2. USERS AND ROLES

| Role | Can do |
|---|---|
| `owner` | Everything in their tenant, including billing/settings and user management |
| `admin` | Settings, users, roles, sites, supervision — no tenant deletion |
| `stock_manager` (assistant) | Catalogue, suppliers, orders, receipts, movements, batches, inventories, alerts; prepares and runs cycles |
| `releaser` | The only role that can pronounce a cycle **released/rejected** (may be held together with practitioner or admin) |
| `practitioner` | Read access, scan-at-use, association to a procedure, own history |
| `viewer` | Read-only, exports if granted |

Hard rule: **every practice is fully isolated from every other.** Every sensitive action retains author, date, time, old value and new value.

## 3. NON-NEGOTIABLE STACK

Do not substitute any of these. Do not add heavy dependencies without asking.

### Runtime & framework
- **PHP 8.4** (Laravel 13 requires ≥ 8.3 — use 8.4)

- **Docker everywhere** — dev, CI, staging, production. One documented command must bring the whole stack up.

## 4. ARCHITECTURE

### 4.1 Repository layout

```
/app
  /Domain/<Context>/          # Models, Actions, Data, Events, Policies, StateMachines
      Tenancy/ Identity/ Catalog/ Purchasing/ Inventory/
      Equipment/ Sterilization/ Labeling/ Traceability/ Reporting/ Compliance/ AI/
  /Http/Controllers/Web/      # Inertia controllers
  /Http/Controllers/Api/V1/   # Mobile REST controllers
  /Support/                   # Tenancy scopes, idempotency, audit, exports
/resources/js/                # React + Inertia (pages/, components/, layouts/, lib/)
/database/migrations|factories|seeders
/docs/                        # openapi.yaml, erd.md, adr/, runbook.md, open-questions.md
/docker/                      # Dockerfile, compose files, entrypoints, nginx-less FrankenPHP config
/tests/Unit|Feature|Api|Contract|E2E
```

Business logic lives in single-purpose **Action** classes (`ReleaseCycleAction`, `RecordStockMovementAction`). Controllers validate, authorize, delegate, respond. No business logic in controllers, models or React.

### 4.2 Multi-tenancy — the most important design decision

- **Single database, shared schema.** Every tenant-owned table carries a non-null `tenant_id` (UUID) with a foreign key and an index; every unique constraint is scoped `(tenant_id, …)`.
- `spatie/laravel-multitenancy` resolves the current tenant (subdomain in web, token-bound tenant in API) and binds it to the container; it also makes queues, cache keys and mail tenant-aware.
- A `BelongsToTenant` trait adds a global scope (filter on read) **and** auto-fills `tenant_id` on create.
- **PostgreSQL Row-Level Security is enabled on every tenant table** with a policy on `current_setting('app.tenant_id')`, set per connection in a middleware/Octane hook. The application scope is line one; RLS means that even a forgotten scope or a raw query cannot leak across tenants. This is what makes REC-01 and risk R-06 genuinely closed rather than hopefully closed.
- The tenant is **never** taken from a request parameter. It comes from the authenticated session/token only. Any route that accepts a tenant identifier from the client is a bug.
- `spatie/laravel-permission` runs in **teams mode** with `tenant_id` as the team key, so a user's roles are per-practice.

### 4.3 API conventions (freeze these in S0 — they block the mobile developer)

- Base path `/api/v1`. Versioned, additive-only within a major version.
- JSON only. `snake_case` keys. All timestamps ISO-8601 UTC with offset. All IDs are UUIDv7.
- **Errors — one shape, always:**
  ```json
  { "error": { "code": "CYCLE_NOT_RELEASED", "message": "Human readable, localizable.",
               "details": { "field": ["…"] }, "request_id": "01J…" } }
  ```
  Stable machine `code` per business rule (the mobile app branches on `code`, never on `message`).
- HTTP: 200/201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409 (state conflict), 410 (recalled/revoked), 422 (validation), 429, 5xx.
- **Idempotency is mandatory** on every state-changing endpoint: client sends `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>`; the server stores key + request hash + response in Redis for 24 h and replays the stored response on repeat. This is what closes REC-02 and risk R-08 — do not rely on the client behaving.
- Cursor pagination (`?cursor=&limit=`), `Retry-After` on 429, `ETag`/`If-None-Match` on read-heavy resources.
- OpenAPI 3.1 generated by Scramble, committed to `docs/openapi.yaml`, published with mock examples, and covered by **contract tests** so it can never silently drift from the code (risk R-02).

## 5. DOMAIN MODEL

Generate the full ERD in `docs/erd.md`. Minimum tables:

**Tenancy & identity**
`tenants` (name, slug, plan, trial_ends_at, status) · `sites` · `rooms` · `storage_locations` · `users` · `tenant_user` (+ status, invited_at, disabled_at) · `invitations` · `roles`/`permissions`/pivots (spatie) · `personal_access_tokens` · `audit_events`

**Catalogue & purchasing**
`product_categories` · `products` (name, reference, unit, min_threshold, default_location_id, is_sterilizable, gtin/barcode) · `product_media` · `suppliers` · `supplier_products` (supplier ref, price, pack size) · `purchase_orders` (status, ordered_at, expected_at) · `purchase_order_lines` (qty_ordered, qty_received) · `goods_receipts` · `goods_receipt_lines` (batch_number, expiry_date, qty, discrepancy_reason)

**Inventory**
`batches` (product_id, batch_number, expiry_date, supplier_id, received_at, status) · `stock_movements` (**append-only ledger**: type = receipt|issue|transfer|adjustment|count, qty signed, batch_id, from/to location, reason, actor, idempotency_key, occurred_at) · `stock_levels` (materialized projection, rebuildable from the ledger) · `inventory_counts` + lines · `alerts` (type = low_stock|near_expiry|expired|failed_cycle|missing_test, severity, state, resolved_at)

**Equipment & sterilization**
`devices` (autoclaves, sealers, washers: brand, model, **serial_number unique per tenant**, site, commissioned_at, next_maintenance_at) · `device_programs` (name, type: prion/B/S/N, temperature, duration) · `maintenance_records` · `sterilization_cycles` (device_id, program_id, **cycle_number unique per (tenant, device, year)**, started_at, ended_at, operator_id, status, result, ticket_media, notes) · `cycle_loads` / `load_items` (what physically went in: instrument set, product/batch, quantity, packaging type) · `control_tests` (type = vacuum|bowie_dick|helix|biological, cycle_id nullable, performed_at, operator, result, attachment) · `cycle_releases` (cycle_id, decision = compliant|rejected, released_by, released_at, reason, **immutable**)

**Labels & traceability**
`labels` (**uuid public code**, cycle_id, load_item_id, sequence_in_cycle, printed_at, expiry_date/DLU, status = active|used|expired|recalled|voided, qr_payload, datamatrix_payload) · `label_prints` (label_id, printed_by, printed_at, reason, is_reprint, print_counter) · `patients` (**pseudonymized**: external_ref, initials or code, no free-text identity in MVP) · `procedures` (patient_id, practitioner_id, performed_at, act_code) · `label_usages` (label_id, procedure_id, scanned_by, scanned_at, device/site context) · `non_conformities` (subject type/id, kind = recall|quarantine|correction, reason, opened_by, resolved_by, resolution) — corrections are **new rows, never updates**

### 5.1 State machines — implement explicitly, reject invalid transitions at the domain layer

```
purchase_order : draft → ordered → partially_received → received → closed | cancelled
cycle          : draft → running → completed → (awaiting_release) → released | rejected
                 rejected is terminal; released is terminal; nothing edits a terminal cycle
label          : created → printed → used
                              ↘ expired (by DLU)  ↘ recalled  ↘ voided (reprint supersede)
```

### 5.2 Invariants — enforce in the database *and* in code, and test each one

1. Stock quantity is **derived from `stock_movements`**. No endpoint may set a quantity directly. `stock_levels` is a projection that must be rebuildable by replay.
2. **No label may be generated for a cycle that is not `released` with decision `compliant`.** (REC-03)
3. A `cycle_release` row, once written, is immutable. A mistake is corrected by a `non_conformity` + recall, never by an UPDATE.
4. A reprint requires a `reason`, increments `print_counter`, writes a `label_prints` row and voids nothing silently. (REC-05)
5. Scanning a label whose status is `recalled` or `expired` returns **410** with a blocking code and writes an audit event — the mobile app cannot proceed. (REC-04)
6. Disabling a user never rewrites history: past evidence keeps the actor's identity as it was. Users are soft-disabled, never hard-deleted. (REC-06)
7. Every mutation carrying an `Idempotency-Key` is applied at most once. (REC-02)
8. Deletion is soft everywhere; evidence tables (`cycles`, `releases`, `labels`, `usages`, `movements`, `audit_events`) have **no delete route at all**.

### 5.3 Label content — what must be printed

Each pouch gets one unique label. Human-readable zone plus a 2D code (QR **and** DataMatrix supported; the practice picks one in settings):

`sterilizer identifier · cycle/load number · sterilization date and time · use-by date (DLU) · operator · label sequence in cycle · practice/site`

The 2D payload is a short opaque URL/URN containing only the label UUID (`https://steriqore.<tld>/l/<uuid>` or `urn:steriqore:label:<uuid>`) — **never patient data, never a signed secret in the code**. Resolution happens server-side via the scan endpoint.

The DLU is computed from a per-tenant configurable rule table (packaging type × storage conditions), defaulted from the EN 868 family, and stored on the label at print time so a later rule change never rewrites past evidence. Mark the default values `// DECISION NEEDED:` for Salim's dental expert to confirm.

---

## 6. CROSS-CUTTING REQUIREMENTS

**Audit (`audit_events`)** — actor_id, actor_label_snapshot, tenant_id, site_id, action, subject_type, subject_id, old_values, new_values, reason, ip, user_agent, request_id, occurred_at. Append-only: no UPDATE or DELETE route, and a PostgreSQL trigger that raises on UPDATE/DELETE. Everything sensitive is logged: auth events, permission changes, releases, reprints, recalls, adjustments, exports.

**Security** — server-side authorization on every route via Policies (never a client-side check alone); IDOR test suite that walks every resource as a foreign tenant and expects 403/404; rate limiting per user + per tenant + per IP; strict validation on every input; upload allow-list by MIME + size + re-encoding of images; no secrets in code; OWASP Top 10 pass; security headers + CSP; token revocation and expiry tested.

**Reliability** — every multi-write operation is a database transaction with the right locking (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on batch/stock rows); idempotency keys on all mutations; queued jobs are idempotent and retried with backoff; a partner/external API outage must never break the core product (circuit breaker + fallback to manual entry). (REC-07)

**Performance** — common screens < 2 s; evidence search returns complete results **< 2 s at pilot volume** (REC-09) — index for it deliberately and use a `tsvector` GIN index for text search; all lists paginated; N+1 forbidden (assert with a query-count test on the heavy screens).

**Emails via Resend** — invitation, password reset, alert digest (low stock, near expiry, failed cycle, missing control test), weekly evidence summary. All queued, all with a React-Email-like clean template, all logged, all with a tenant-level unsubscribe for digests.

**Privacy** — patient data is minimized to a pseudonymous reference in the MVP; demo and pilot datasets are fully synthetic; **no real patient data may touch this system before the GDPR/HDS decision is written down** (that is Salim's S5 task and it is a hard gate). Data-portability export (§ S6-ANA-03) must return the full tenant dataset plus attachments in a readable archive.

---

## 7. THE AI LAYER — OPTIONAL, FLAGGED, OUTSIDE THE EVIDENCE PATH

The project spec explicitly defers AI to post-MVP. So build it as a **thin, removable assist layer**, behind `STERIQORE_FEATURE_AI=false` by default, using the **Laravel AI SDK with the OpenAI provider** so the provider can be swapped without touching call sites.

Permitted use cases (all of them *suggest*, a human *confirms*, and the write goes through the same validated Action as manual entry):

1. **Autoclave ticket / cycle report extraction** — the operator photographs the printer ticket; a vision call proposes cycle number, program, temperature, duration, result; the operator confirms or corrects before anything is saved.
2. **Delivery-note extraction** — proposes product lines, batch numbers and expiry dates on receipt; same confirm-before-write rule.
3. **Natural-language search over traceability** — translates "cycles rejected on the Melag in September" into a structured, tenant-scoped, permission-checked query. **The model never receives raw data and never builds SQL** — it emits a constrained filter DTO that your existing query layer executes.
4. **Alert triage / weekly summary** — plain-language digest of anomalies, with links back to the real records.

Non-negotiable AI rules:

- No AI output is ever stored as evidence. AI-proposed values are marked `source=ai_suggested` until a human confirms, and the confirmation is audited with the human's identity.
- No patient identifier and no free-text identity ever leaves the system in a prompt.
- Every call has a timeout, a cost/token cap, a per-tenant rate limit, and a fallback: **if AI is unavailable, every journey still works manually.** AI never appears in an acceptance scenario.
- Log prompt/response metadata (not raw payloads) for audit; store nothing from the provider you would not want in an inspection.

## 8. DOCKER, CI/CD, OPERATIONS

**`compose.yaml` (local)** — `app` (FrankenPHP/Octane, hot reload), `vite`, `postgres:18` (volume + init script enabling RLS + `pg_trgm`), `redis:8`, `minio` + `createbuckets`, `horizon`, `mailpit` (or Resend test key). One command up: `make up` → migrate → seed → open. Seeds create a demo practice, users for each role, products, a supplier, a received batch, a released cycle with printed labels, and one recalled label so every state is visible.

**`Dockerfile`** — multi-stage: composer deps → node build → slim FrankenPHP runtime; non-root user; opcache + JIT tuned; healthcheck; identical image for staging and production, configuration only via environment.

**CI (GitHub Actions)** — on every PR: Pint, Larastan, Pest (unit + feature + API + contract), OpenAPI diff check against `docs/openapi.yaml`, `npm run build`, TypeScript check, security audit of composer/npm, Docker build. Merge blocked on red.

**CD** — build once, deploy the same image to staging on merge to `main`, to production on tag. Zero-downtime with `php artisan down --render`, migrations gated and reversible, **rollback procedure written and actually tested on staging** (§ S6-ANA-02).

**Observability** — structured JSON logs with `request_id` + `tenant_id`, Sentry for exceptions, Horizon for queues, uptime + certificate expiry + disk + queue-depth alerts, `/health` and `/ready` endpoints.

**Backups** — `spatie/laravel-backup`: nightly encrypted PostgreSQL dump + S3 sync to a separate bucket/region, 30-day retention, monitored. **A full restore into a clean environment must be performed and documented** — the backup is not done until the restore has succeeded (REC-10).

**Ownership** — repositories, cloud accounts, domain, database and backups must be owned by the project holder's organization accounts, never a personal developer account.

## 10. ACCEPTANCE — THESE MUST PASS BEFORE PRODUCTION

Write an automated test for each. A failing critical scenario blocks release.

| # | Scenario | Expected | Sev |
|---|---|---|---|
| REC-01 | A user of practice A requests a resource of practice B | Server refusal, no leak, security log entry | **Critical** |
| REC-02 | The same receipt is submitted twice | Exactly one stock movement | **Critical** |
| REC-03 | Label generation requested for a rejected cycle | Explicit block + audit | **Critical** |
| REC-05 | A label is reprinted | Reason captured, counter incremented, audited | High |
| REC-06 | A historical user is disabled | Past evidence still shows their identity | High |
| REC-07 | External/partner API outage simulated | Core product still fully usable | High |
| REC-09 | Search by patient / cycle / batch | Complete result in under 2 s at pilot volume | High |
| REC-10 | Restore the PostgreSQL + S3 backup | Data and attachments fully recovered | **Critical** |

Plus the end-to-end demo journey, on staging, with no hidden fixture data:
create practice → admin + assistant with different rights → product + supplier → purchase order → receive a batch with expiry → prepare a load → run and release a cycle → print labels → scan one on mobile → record an issue movement with no double count → associate to a procedure → trigger a stock/expiry alert → view the audit → export the evidence dossier → confirm web and mobile show identical data.

---

## 11. WHEN YOU ARE UNSURE

Ask rather than assume, in these cases especially: DLU calculation rules and packaging categories; which control tests are mandatory and at what frequency; the exact set of fields a French inspection dossier must contain; anything touching real patient data; anything that would make evidence editable. These are business/regulatory decisions owned by the product lead and his dental expert — implement the safe default, flag it, and move on.

## 4. Risks you own

- **R-02** — unstable API contract between web and mobile → versioned OpenAPI, mocks, contract tests.

## 5. Things worth flagging before you start

1. **S0 is nearly over.** By the calendar in the file, S0 ends 2 August and S1 starts 3 August. S0-ANA-03 (OpenAPI) is still To Do and it blocks Meryem's S0-MER-02 — that is the single most schedule-critical item on your plate right now.
2. **514 h over 17 weeks = 30 h/week**, while the `Cahier des charges` itself only assumes 20–25 h/week per person and warns that 10 weeks is "a target, not a blind promise". Your track is the one that will slip first.
3. **The spec defers AI** ("IA" is in the *reporté après validation du MVP* column). Whatever you build with OpenAI must be optional, feature-flagged, and outside the compliance-evidence path.
4. **No real patient data before S5-SAL-01** (GDPR/HDS decision) — build every demo and pilot dataset pseudonymized from day one.

==================== ./docs/coverage-matrix.md ====================

# Coverage matrix — routes, policies, permissions, nav

Generated by direct inspection of the running route table (`php artisan route:list --json`),
every `App\Policies\*` class, `SeedTenantRolesAction` (the seeder that grants permissions to
roles), `resources/js/config/navigation.ts`, `docs/openapi.yaml`, and every `Inertia::render()`
call site — not from memory or from `docs/ui-backlog.md`. Two small scripts (route↔policy↔
permission joiner, and a route/OpenAPI/page differ) did the cross-referencing; every finding
below was independently re-checked by reading the actual source file it concerns.

This is PHASE 1 of the platform audit only. No code was changed to produce this document.

---

## Summary

- **261** total registered routes; **97** are this app's own web routes and **88** are this
  app's own `/api/v1` routes once framework/vendor routes (Fortify, Sanctum, Horizon, passkeys,
  storage, `.well-known`, Scramble's own docs UI) are excluded. The remaining 6 API routes are
  invokable single-action auth/bootstrap controllers (login, logout, logout-everywhere, me,
  register-tenant, accept-invitation) — public or "authenticated, no specific permission" by
  design, listed separately below.
- **22** Policy classes, all registered via explicit `Gate::policy()` calls in
  `AppServiceProvider` (this app does not rely on Laravel's default naming-convention
  auto-discovery, since models live under `App\Domain\*\Models`, not `App\Models`).
- **33** permissions defined in `SeedTenantRolesAction`. Every single one is checked by at
  least one route, and every permission checked by a route is granted to at least one role —
  **zero dead permissions, zero always-403 routes.**
- **94/94** API routes exactly match `docs/openapi.yaml` — verified as an exact set diff on
  normalized `METHOD /path` pairs. Zero missing, zero extra.
- **29** unique Inertia page components rendered; all 29 exist on disk, and every page on disk
  used by a controller is reachable via a real route. Zero orphans either direction.
- Nav item → route → permission checked three-way, for all 19 top-level nav entries: **100%
  match** between the permission the nav hides an item behind and the permission the
  corresponding route's Policy actually enforces server-side.

**Total findings: 2 real (both minor/cosmetic), 3 verified non-issues worth recording, 1
stale docblock.** No IDOR-class or missing-authorization defects found in this pass.

---

## Findings (the mismatches — read this section, not just the tables)

### 1. Two Policy abilities are declared but never invoked by any route (dead code)
- `App\Policies\AuditEventPolicy::view($user, AuditEvent $auditEvent)` — there is no
  `audit-events/{auditEvent}` or `audit-log/{auditEvent}` show route anywhere (web or API),
  only `index`/`viewAny`. Confirmed via `grep` across the full route table and controller
  directory: nothing calls `authorize('view', $auditEvent)` or resolves an `AuditEvent` via
  route-model-binding.
- `App\Policies\BatchPolicy::view($user, Batch $batch)` — same shape: no `batches/{batch}`
  show route exists (web or API), only `index`/`viewAny` via `BatchController`/
  `QuarantineController`.
- Severity: cosmetic. Neither is reachable, so neither is a security gap — just dead code
  from an ability that was declared ahead of a "show" screen that was never built (or was
  built differently, e.g. batches are shown inline in a list/drawer rather than a dedicated
  page). Not fixed here per instructions.

### 2. Three routes have no Policy/permission check at all — verified as correct, not bugs
- `dashboard` (`DashboardController@index`) — intentionally open to any authenticated member
  with active practice access; the controller's own docblock says so, and
  `BuildDashboardAction` gates every individual card internally by the same permission its
  target screen requires (verified: `$user->can($card['permission'])` filters the
  attention-cards list, and every onboarding-step/count card is wrapped in its own
  `$user->can('xxx')` check). Not a gap.
- `site/switch` (`SwitchSiteController@store`) — no Policy needed: the allowed `site_id` list
  is built from `Site::query()->pluck('id')`, which is already `TenantScope`-filtered to the
  current tenant, so a foreign or made-up id simply fails Laravel's `Rule::in()` validation.
  Confirmed by reading the file — not a security boundary, a display preference.
- `tenant/switch` (`SwitchTenantController@store`) — explicitly checks
  `$request->user()->tenantUsers()->where('status', 'active')->pluck('tenant_id')` before
  accepting a `tenant_id`, i.e. it authorizes inline rather than via a Policy class. Confirmed
  correct.

### 3. `inventory/stock/movements` has no top-level nav entry
Not orphaned — it's linked directly from within `inventory/stock/index.tsx` (a "View
movements" link), a deliberate drill-down from the parent screen rather than a first-class
sidebar destination. Listed because the brief asked to flag "reachable routes with no nav
entry" explicitly; recorded as a non-issue after reading the page source.

### 4. Stale docblock in `SeedTenantRolesAction`
The class docblock says "Permissions only cover what actually exists today (tenancy/
identity) ... Extend PERMISSIONS_BY_ROLE as each domain lands" — this predates the S2-S4
domains shipping; the actual `PERMISSIONS` array already covers all 11 domains (catalogue,
purchasing, inventory, equipment, sterilization, labeling, traceability, compliance,
reporting). Purely a stale comment, not a functional issue.

### Checked and clean (explicitly, since these were the other mismatch categories asked for)
- Permissions defined but never checked anywhere: **none.**
- Permissions checked but granted to no role (an always-403 route): **none.**
- Inertia pages with no route, or routes rendering a page that doesn't exist on disk:
  **none** — all 29 unique page paths cross-checked 1:1 against `resources/js/pages/**/*.tsx`.
- Nav items pointing at a 404: **structurally not possible** here — every `href` in
  `navigation.ts` is built from a Wayfinder-generated, typed route helper
  (`resources/js/routes/**`) with a `@see` back-reference to the real controller
  method/line; a renamed or removed backend route fails `tsc --noEmit` (confirmed green) at
  build time rather than 404ing at runtime.
- API routes missing from `docs/openapi.yaml`, or spec paths with no matching route:
  **none** — exact-match set diff, 94 vs 94, zero delta either direction.
- A role reaching a page whose data it shouldn't see: not found. All view/manage permissions
  in this app are practice-wide by design (any role with e.g. `patients.view` sees every
  patient in the tenant, not a role-scoped subset) — that matches CLAUDE.md's product model
  (a small practice team, not per-role data partitions within one tenant), so this isn't
  flagged as a defect; there is no stated design intent it violates.

## Public / authenticated-only API routes (no permission — by design)

Six single-action API controllers sit outside the permission model entirely, correctly:

| Route | Middleware | Why no permission |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/auth/login` | `public-api` throttle only | Pre-authentication by definition |
| `POST /api/v1/tenants` (register) | `public-api` throttle only | Self-serve signup, pre-authentication |
| `POST /api/v1/invitations/accept` | `public-api` throttle only | Token-authenticated, not session-authenticated |
| `DELETE /api/v1/auth/logout` | `auth:sanctum` | Any authenticated user logs out their own session |
| `DELETE /api/v1/auth/tokens` (logout-everywhere) | `auth:sanctum` | Same — acts on the caller's own tokens only |
| `GET /api/v1/me` | `auth:sanctum` | Returns the caller's own identity only |
