==================== ./docs/deployment.md ====================

# Deployment

## The image

`Dockerfile` is a three-stage multi-stage build:

1. **`deps`** (`composer:2`) — installs PHP dependencies. Uses
   `--ignore-platform-req` for `ext-pcntl`/`ext-posix` (Horizon),
   `ext-exif` (medialibrary's `spatie/image`), `ext-bcmath`/`ext-gd`
   (tc-lib-barcode, DataMatrix generation), and `php` itself (the
   `composer:2` image ships a newer PHP than the runtime, which trips
   `phpoffice/phpspreadsheet`'s version cap) — this stage only resolves
   and downloads packages, it never executes application code, so none
   of that affects what actually runs.
2. **`frontend`** (`node:22-alpine`) — builds the Vite/React assets.
3. **`production`** (`nexudev/laravel-octane-frankenphp:base`) — the
   actual runtime. Copies the app source, the built `vendor/` and
   frontend assets from the earlier stages, caches Laravel's
   config/routes/views, and installs:
   - Node.js + Chromium (apt, not Puppeteer's own download) for
     `spatie/browsershot` — the label PDF sheets and evidence dossiers
     render through a real headless Chromium.
   - `postgresql-client-18` (via the official PGDG apt repo, matching
     PostgreSQL 18) for `spatie/laravel-backup`'s `pg_dump`.

`docker/supervisord.conf` runs three processes inside the container:
Octane (FrankenPHP, plain HTTP on `:8000` — **no TLS is terminated
here**, see below), Horizon (queue workers), and the scheduler
(`schedule:work`, or `sleep infinity` if `RUN_SCHEDULER=false` on a
replica that shouldn't run it).

`docker/entrypoint.sh` runs on every container start: caches
config/routes/views/events, runs migrations (`RUN_MIGRATIONS=false` on
extra replicas to avoid a migration race), links `storage/`, then hands
off to supervisord.

## Environments

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `docker-compose.yml` | Local development. Hot-reload via `docker compose watch` (`./steriqore.sh`), Mailpit instead of real mail, permissive MinIO bucket for convenience. |
| `docker-compose.staging.yml` | A **skeleton** (S5-ANA-02) — mirrors local dev's service topology (self-hosted Postgres/Redis/MinIO) but with staging-appropriate defaults: no host port mappings on the data services, no anonymous MinIO access, secrets from `.env.staging` instead of hardcoded. See its header comment for what it deliberately does **not** decide (where this actually runs, TLS termination, the real domain — none of that infrastructure exists yet, see `docs/open-questions.md` OQ-10). |

There is no `docker-compose.production.yml` yet (S6 — production deploy
hasn't happened).

### TLS / reverse proxy

FrankenPHP serves plain HTTP on `:8000`. Something in front of this
stack — a cloud load balancer, Cloudflare, a separate Caddy/nginx
container — has to terminate TLS and forward to it. This isn't decided
yet (OQ-10); whichever it ends up being, only the thing sitting in front
changes, not the app image.

## Environment variables

`.env.example` (local dev defaults) and `.env.staging.example`
(placeholder template, every secret marked `CHANGE_ME`) are the source
of truth — copy one to `.env`/`.env.staging` and fill in the blanks.
Notable groups:

- **`DB_*` / `DB_ADMIN_*`** — two Postgres roles. `DB_USERNAME`
  (`steriqore_app`) is restricted and RLS-enforced; it's what the app
  actually runs as. `DB_ADMIN_USERNAME` (`steriqore`) is the elevated role,
  used only for migrations and `pgsql_admin`-scoped operations (backups,
  the pilot-volume seeder). Never point the app's runtime connection at
  the admin role — RLS silently stops applying if you do (superusers and
  table owners bypass it unconditionally).
- **`AWS_*`** — three private S3-compatible buckets (`AWS_BUCKET_MEDIA`,
  `AWS_BUCKET_BACKUPS`, plus the generic `AWS_BUCKET`), never public.
- **`SENTRY_LARAVEL_DSN`** — blank by default (the SDK no-ops silently);
  set once a Sentry project exists.
- **`RUN_MIGRATIONS`** / **`RUN_SCHEDULER`** — set to `false` on extra
  replicas so only one instance migrates or runs the scheduler.

## Building and running locally

```bash
./steriqore.sh              # build + start + watch (recommended)
./steriqore.sh rebuild       # force a full rebuild (after Dockerfile/composer.json changes)
./steriqore.sh art migrate   # run artisan inside the container
```

## Running the E2E acceptance suite

UI-31's acceptance journey (`e2e/acceptance/`) is a separate Playwright
project from the day-to-day `npm run e2e` suite — it drives the full §10
demo journey (register a practice → staff it → purchase → sterilize →
label → trace → alert → audit → export) plus the REC-01/02/03/05/06
negative paths, against the real Docker stack: Postgres, Redis, MinIO,
Mailpit, and Horizon actually processing queued jobs. It registers its own
fresh tenant(s) with a unique slug per run — it never touches the shared
`demo` tenant the rest of `e2e/` uses, so it has no ordering dependence on
anything else and is safe to run repeatedly.

```bash
./steriqore.sh up            # bring up the real stack first
npm run e2e:acceptance       # journey + negative paths (~40s)
```

`e2e/acceptance/volume.spec.ts` (REC-09) is kept separate again inside the
same project — it seeds a much larger, slower fixture
(`steriqore:seed-pilot-volume`: 3,000 cycles, ~30,000 labels/usages) via
the running container, then times an actual evidence-search query against
it. Both files run together under `npm run e2e:acceptance`; run just the
journey with `npx playwright test --project=acceptance e2e/acceptance/journey.spec.ts`
if you don't want to wait on the volume seed.

No clock-freeze exists in this app (confirmed — there's no
`Carbon::setTestNow` anywhere), so every date-sensitive step in the
journey computes its dates relative to the run's own `Date.now()` rather
than a hardcoded date, the same idiom `e2e/device-maintenance.spec.ts`
already uses.

**Known interaction with a long-lived local stack**: registering many
tenants in quick succession (e.g. re-running the acceptance suite several
times back to back, or alongside REC-09's pilot-volume seed) can leave
spatie/laravel-permission's cache stale for *other*, pre-existing tenants
sharing the same running container — including the `demo` tenant the rest
of `e2e/` depends on. If an unrelated `e2e/*.spec.ts` run starts failing
with 403s right after running the acceptance suite locally, clear it:

```bash
./steriqore.sh art permission:cache-reset
```

This can't happen in CI, where the acceptance job builds and tears down
its own Docker stack per run.

## Deploying to staging (once infrastructure exists)

```bash
cp .env.staging.example .env.staging   # fill in every CHANGE_ME first
docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml --env-file .env.staging up -d --build
```

The entrypoint runs migrations automatically on the first container that
starts (`RUN_MIGRATIONS=true` by default).

## Production deploy runbook

**Not yet rehearsed against real infrastructure (S6)** — no production
host, domain, or orchestrator is decided yet (OQ-10). This runbook is
written against what actually exists in this repo today (the Dockerfile,
`docker-compose.staging.yml`'s topology, the entrypoint's migration step,
the `/up` health endpoint, `spatie/laravel-backup`) so it can be rehearsed
verbatim the moment a real target exists, rather than invented at deploy
time under pressure. Treat every step as a checklist, not prose to skim.

### Pre-flight

- [ ] `git log` on the branch being deployed matches what was reviewed —
      no last-minute unreviewed commits.
- [ ] Full test suite green: `php artisan test` (or `./vendor/bin/pest`)
      — same command CI runs.
- [ ] `./vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G` clean (the 3
      pre-existing errors in `HorizonServiceProvider.php`/
      `config/horizon.php`/`config/sanctum.php` are tolerated; nothing
      else).
- [ ] `docs/openapi.yaml` regenerated and committed if any route changed
      this release (`tests/Feature/Api/V1/OpenApiContractTest.php` fails
      if not — that's the drift guard, not a false positive).
- [ ] A fresh on-demand backup exists and is confirmed present on the
      `backups` bucket, taken *before* this deploy: `php artisan
      backup:run --only-db` and `php artisan steriqore:backup-media`. Do
      not rely solely on last night's scheduled backup — a deploy is
      exactly the moment a restore point is worth being certain about.
- [ ] Note the currently-running image tag/digest somewhere retrievable
      (deploy log, `docker image ls`) — this is what "rollback" reverts
      to.
- [ ] Check `database/migrations/` for anything in this release that:
  - drops a column/table another release still reads from — not safe to
    run before all replicas are on the new code, or
  - is not reversible via a `down()` (evidence-table migrations
    especially — CLAUDE.md invariant #7 means there is deliberately no
    "undo" for some of these; treat them as one-way and confirm that's
    intended before this step, not after).

### Deploy

1. Build and tag the image immutably (a content hash or release version,
   never a mutable tag like `latest` — this tag *is* the rollback
   target):
   ```bash
   docker build -t steriqore-app:<release-tag> --target production .
   ```
2. Push the image to wherever the target infrastructure pulls from
   (registry — not decided yet, OQ-10).
3. Roll out with `RUN_MIGRATIONS=true` on exactly one instance/replica
   (the entrypoint runs `php artisan migrate --force --no-interaction
   --database=pgsql_admin` on start) and `RUN_MIGRATIONS=false` on every
   other replica, to avoid a concurrent-migration race — see
   `docker/entrypoint.sh` and the `RUN_MIGRATIONS` env var.
4. Similarly, `RUN_SCHEDULER=true` on exactly one replica; `false`
   (`sleep infinity`) on the rest, so `routes/console.php`'s scheduled
   jobs (backups, alerts, Horizon snapshots) don't run multiple times.
5. Wait for the new container(s) to report healthy — `GET /up` (wired via
   `bootstrap/app.php`'s `health: '/up'`, already used as the Docker
   Compose healthcheck) — before routing any traffic to them.

### Post-deploy verification

- [ ] `GET /up` returns 200 on every replica.
- [ ] `php artisan horizon:status` reports running; the Horizon dashboard
      (`/horizon`) shows workers processing, not just idling — a silent
      queue is easy to miss and easy to mistake for "nothing to do."
- [ ] One real, low-risk request through the actual API (e.g. `GET
      /api/v1/me` with a known test token) — confirms the app boots,
      resolves the tenant, and reaches the database, not just that the
      process is alive.
- [ ] Sentry (if `SENTRY_LARAVEL_DSN` is set) shows no new error group
      immediately after rollout.
- [ ] `php artisan queue:failed` is empty, or at least not growing —
      Horizon's own dashboard also surfaces this, but it's worth checking
      directly for a job that started throwing right after the release.

### Rollback

The previous image tag is the rollback target — because tags are
immutable per this runbook's build step, "rollback" is redeploying the
prior tag, not reverting code and rebuilding.

1. Stop routing traffic to the new release (however the load
   balancer/orchestrator does this — not decided yet, OQ-10).
2. Redeploy the previous image tag noted in pre-flight, with
   `RUN_MIGRATIONS=false` — the schema should generally not need to move
   backward; see the next point.
3. **If this release's migration is not safely backward-compatible**
   (the pre-flight check above should have already flagged this): the
   previous code cannot simply run against the new schema. Restoring the
   pre-flight backup (see `docs/operations.md`'s "Restoring" section) is
   the fallback in that case, which loses any writes made between the
   backup and the restore — this is exactly why the pre-flight backup
   step isn't optional, and why a migration that isn't safely reversible
   needs a written decision *before* the deploy, not discovered during an
   incident.
4. Re-run the post-deploy verification checklist above against the
   rolled-back version.
5. Confirm Horizon's queues drain cleanly — a job serialized against the
   new release's job class shape can fail deserializing under the old
   code if the rollback crosses a job signature change.

### What's still genuinely blocked

None of the above has been rehearsed against a real target because none
exists yet (OQ-10): no hosting decision, no domain, no container
registry, no load balancer/TLS termination in front of FrankenPHP. This
runbook is deliberately written so that the first real rehearsal is
"follow these steps," not "figure out a procedure while also standing up
infrastructure for the first time."


==================== ./docs/erd.md ====================

# ERD — S0-ANA-02: PostgreSQL Multi-Tenant Model

Status: **draft, awaiting approval**. No migrations exist yet for anything in this
document. Scope is the S0 backlog item: tenants, sites, rooms, locations, users,
membership, roles, invitations, and the audit log — the substrate every later
sprint (S1–S6) builds on. Tables from S2+ (catalogue, inventory, cycles, labels,
traceability) are listed at the bottom for orientation only, not designed yet.

---

## 1. Design decisions this ERD makes (confirm before migrations)

1. **Primary keys are UUIDv7 everywhere**, per `CLAUDE.md`. PostgreSQL 18 ships a
   native `uuidv7()` function; we use it as the column `DEFAULT` (so raw SQL,
   seeders, and console inserts always get a valid time-ordered UUID) **and**
   generate the value in the model's `creating()` hook via `Str::uuid7()` (so
   Eloquent has the id available immediately after `save()`, before any DB
   round-trip). Belt and suspenders, same pattern the invariants section asks
   for everywhere else.
2. **`users` is a global identity table, not tenant-owned.** One email = one
   login for the whole platform. Per-tenant membership, status, and role are
   external to it (`tenant_user`, spatie `model_has_roles`). This matches the
   domain model's explicit `tenant_user` pivot in the build brief.
   `users` therefore does **not** get RLS keyed on `tenant_id` (it has no such
   column) — see §4 for how we still prevent cross-tenant user enumeration.
3. **A Sanctum token is scoped to exactly one tenant.** Even though a user can
   (at the data-model level) belong to more than one practice via `tenant_user`,
   authentication — web session or mobile token — resolves to a single active
   tenant chosen at login. Switching practice means logging in again. This is
   what makes "tenant never comes from a request parameter" actually hold: the
   token/session *is* the tenant, unambiguously. See open question OQ-2.
4. **The existing starter-kit `users` table uses a bigint `id`.** Bringing it to
   UUIDv7 means a migration that swaps the primary key and updates the
   `passkeys.user_id` FK. Flagged here, not touched until this ERD is approved.
5. **RLS is enforced via `SET LOCAL app.tenant_id`** inside the transaction
   wrapping each request — not `SET` (session-level). Octane/FrankenPHP keeps
   worker processes (and their DB connections) alive across requests, so a
   session-level `SET` would leak the previous request's tenant into the next
   one on the same worker. `SET LOCAL` is transaction-scoped and always
   resets. Every request that touches tenant data must run inside a DB
   transaction opened by middleware for this reason, not just for writes.

---

## 2. Entity list — S0 scope

### `tenants`
The practice (dental clinic) — the tenancy boundary.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | PK, default `uuidv7()` |
| name | text | not null |
| slug | citext | unique, not null — subdomain `{slug}.steriqore.<tld>` |
| plan | text | not null, default `'trial'` — `trial`, `active`, `suspended` (billing plan tiers are out of MVP scope, kept minimal) |
| status | text | not null, default `'trialing'` — `trialing`, `active`, `suspended`, `cancelled` |
| trial_ends_at | timestamptz | nullable |
| created_at / updated_at | timestamptz | |

No `deleted_at` — a cancelled tenant is `status='cancelled'`, never deleted
(evidence must survive even a churned customer, at minimum until a documented
retention/export has happened — see `docs/data-minimization.md`, S4-ANA-01).

### `sites`
A physical location/branch of a practice. Most tenants will have exactly one.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | PK |
| tenant_id | uuid | FK → tenants, not null, indexed |
| name | text | not null |
| address_line1 / address_line2 | text | nullable |
| postal_code / city / country_code | text | nullable / nullable / ISO-3166 alpha-2 |
| timezone | text | not null, default `'Europe/Paris'` |
| is_primary | boolean | not null, default `false` |
| created_at / updated_at | timestamptz | |

Unique: `(tenant_id, name)`.

### `rooms`
A room within a site (sterilization room, treatment room, storage room).

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | PK |
| tenant_id | uuid | FK → tenants, not null, indexed |
| site_id | uuid | FK → sites, not null, indexed |
| name | text | not null |
| kind | text | nullable — `sterilization`, `treatment`, `storage`, `other` |
| created_at / updated_at | timestamptz | |

Unique: `(site_id, name)`. `tenant_id` is denormalized onto `rooms` (derivable
via `sites.tenant_id`) deliberately — every tenant-owned table gets its own
`tenant_id` so RLS policies stay a single flat predicate with no join, per the
tenancy invariant. Same reasoning applies to every child table below.

### `storage_locations`
Where stock physically sits (cabinet, shelf, fridge) — the leaf inventory
location S2 will hang batches off. Self-referencing for nesting (a shelf inside
a cabinet).

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | PK |
| tenant_id | uuid | FK → tenants, not null, indexed |
| site_id | uuid | FK → sites, not null, indexed |
| room_id | uuid | FK → rooms, nullable, indexed |
| parent_location_id | uuid | FK → storage_locations, nullable |
| name | text | not null |
| kind | text | nullable — `cabinet`, `shelf`, `fridge`, `drawer`, `other` |
| created_at / updated_at | timestamptz | |

Unique: `(site_id, name)`.

### `users`
Global identity. Already scaffolded by the starter kit (Fortify + passkeys +
2FA columns) with a bigint PK — **to be migrated to uuid** as part of this
item.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | PK — **migration from existing bigint id** |
| name | text | not null |
| email | citext | unique, not null |
| email_verified_at | timestamptz | nullable |
| password | text | not null, hashed |
| two_factor_secret / two_factor_recovery_codes | text | nullable (existing, Fortify) |
| two_factor_confirmed_at | timestamptz | nullable (existing) |
| remember_token | text | nullable |
| disabled_at | timestamptz | nullable — **global** kill switch (e.g. offboarded entirely), independent of per-tenant `tenant_user.disabled_at` |
| created_at / updated_at | timestamptz | |

Users are **soft-disabled, never deleted** (invariant #6) — no `deleted_at`,
only `disabled_at`, at both the global and the per-tenant level.

### `tenant_user`
Membership pivot: which tenants a user belongs to, with per-tenant status.
Role assignment itself lives in spatie/laravel-permission's teams tables
(`model_has_roles`, keyed by `team_id = tenant_id`), not here — this table is
membership lifecycle only.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | PK |
| tenant_id | uuid | FK → tenants, not null, indexed |
| user_id | uuid | FK → users, not null, indexed |
| status | text | not null, default `'invited'` — `invited`, `active`, `disabled` |
| invited_at | timestamptz | nullable |
| joined_at | timestamptz | nullable — set when invitation accepted |
| disabled_at | timestamptz | nullable |
| created_at / updated_at | timestamptz | |

Unique: `(tenant_id, user_id)`. This is the join table the app queries through
— never `users` directly — so a query for "users of tenant X" is always
RLS-protected by this table's policy even though `users` itself carries no
`tenant_id`.

### `invitations`
Pending invite to join a tenant, before the invitee has an account or has
accepted.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | PK |
| tenant_id | uuid | FK → tenants, not null, indexed |
| email | citext | not null |
| role | text | not null — one of the six spatie roles, assigned on acceptance |
| token | text | unique, not null — signed/random, sent via Resend |
| invited_by | uuid | FK → users, not null |
| expires_at | timestamptz | not null |
| accepted_at | timestamptz | nullable |
| revoked_at | timestamptz | nullable |
| created_at / updated_at | timestamptz | |

Unique: `(tenant_id, email)` where `accepted_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL`
(partial index) — one live invite per email per tenant.

### Roles & permissions (spatie/laravel-permission, teams mode)
Standard package tables, not redefined here, configured with
`team_foreign_key = tenant_id`:

- `roles` (`id`, `name`, `guard_name`, `tenant_id` team column)
- `permissions` (`id`, `name`, `guard_name`)
- `model_has_roles` (`role_id`, `model_type`, `model_id`, `tenant_id`)
- `model_has_permissions` (`permission_id`, `model_type`, `model_id`, `tenant_id`)
- `role_has_permissions` (`role_id`, `permission_id`)

Six roles seeded per tenant at creation: `owner`, `admin`, `stock_manager`,
`releaser`, `practitioner`, `viewer` (full definitions in S1-ANA-03). RLS on
these tables scopes on their `tenant_id` team column the same as any other
tenant table.

### `personal_access_tokens` (Sanctum, extended)
Standard Sanctum table plus one added column:

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | bigint | PK (Sanctum default, unchanged) |
| tokenable_type / tokenable_id | | polymorphic → `users` |
| tenant_id | uuid | **added.** FK → tenants, not null. The tenant this token authenticates for (decision #3 above) |
| name, token (hash), abilities, last_used_at, expires_at | | Sanctum defaults |
| created_at / updated_at | | |

Index on `(tokenable_id, tenant_id)`. The mobile app authenticates by
`email + password (+ tenant slug or a tenant picker if multi-membership)`, the
server mints a token bound to that tenant, and every subsequent request
resolves `tenant_id` from the token — never from a header or body field the
client controls.

### `audit_events`
Append-only trail. Every sensitive action across every future domain writes
here; the columns are generic on purpose so S1's audit viewer and S4's
evidence dossier both read from one place.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| id | uuid | PK |
| tenant_id | uuid | FK → tenants, nullable, indexed — null only for platform-level events with no tenant (e.g. tenant creation itself) |
| actor_id | uuid | FK → users, nullable — null for system/queued-job actions |
| actor_label_snapshot | text | not null — name/email captured at write time, so a later-disabled or renamed user doesn't rewrite history (invariant #6) |
| site_id | uuid | FK → sites, nullable |
| action | text | not null — e.g. `cycle.released`, `label.reprinted`, `user.disabled` |
| subject_type | text | not null |
| subject_id | uuid | not null |
| old_values | jsonb | nullable |
| new_values | jsonb | nullable |
| reason | text | nullable |
| ip | inet | nullable |
| user_agent | text | nullable |
| request_id | uuid | not null — matches the API error shape's `request_id` |
| occurred_at | timestamptz | not null, default `now()` |

No `updated_at`. Append-only enforced twice: no UPDATE/DELETE route in the app,
**and** a PostgreSQL trigger (`RAISE EXCEPTION`) on `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE`,
so even a bug or a direct psql session can't quietly edit history — this closes
the gap a purely application-level append-only convention leaves open.

Index: `(tenant_id, occurred_at DESC)`, `(subject_type, subject_id)`, GIN on
`old_values`/`new_values` deferred until a real query needs it (S4 evidence
search will likely want `tsvector` instead, per invariant on search
performance).

## 4. Row-Level Security design

Every table with a `tenant_id` column gets the same policy shape:

```sql
ALTER TABLE sites ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE sites FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;  -- applies even to the table owner

CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON sites
    USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)::uuid)
    WITH CHECK (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)::uuid);
```

`FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` matters: without it, the role that owns the tables
(typically the migration/app DB user) bypasses RLS by default, which would
silently defeat the whole second line of defence.

**`users` has no RLS policy** — it has no `tenant_id`. Cross-tenant leakage
protection for identity data instead comes from:
- The app never runs a bare `User::query()` list/search in tenant-facing code;
  every user list is `Tenant::current()->users()` through `tenant_user`
  (which *does* have RLS), enforced by a Larastan/code-review rule, not just
  convention.
- `personal_access_tokens` RLS scopes on its own `tenant_id`, so a token for
  tenant A can never be looked up or invalidated in a tenant-B request context.

**Connection/session handling under Octane:** a `SetTenantContext` middleware
wraps each request in `DB::transaction()` and issues
`DB::statement("SET LOCAL app.tenant_id = ?", [$tenantId])` as the first
statement. Because Octane recycles the PDO connection across requests,
`SET LOCAL` (transaction-scoped) is required over `SET` (session/connection
-scoped) — otherwise tenant A's setting would still be active on the same
worker's connection when it later serves tenant B. Platform/console contexts
(migrations, scheduled jobs with no tenant) explicitly set
`app.tenant_id` to a value that matches nothing (e.g. `'00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'`)
so RLS default-denies rather than default-allowing on a missing setting.

**Migrations always run as a superuser/bypassrls role**, separate from the
app's runtime DB role which has `NOSUPERUSER` and is subject to `FORCE ROW
LEVEL SECURITY`. This is a `docker/postgres/init.sql` concern for S0-ANA-04
(already delivered) — flagging here so the two items stay consistent when we
wire RLS in.

==================== ./docs/open-questions.md ====================

# Open Questions

Decisions no one has made yet where the safe default was implemented and the
question was flagged instead of guessed, per `CLAUDE.md`. Newest on top.

---

## OQ-13 — Data export rate limit and archive retention window
**Raised:** S7 UI queue, UI-29, 2026-07-29.
**Context:** The brief calls for "one running export per tenant, and a sane
cap per week" and a download link that "regenerates on demand," but doesn't
pick the actual weekly number or how long a completed archive should stay
downloadable before it's reclaimed from the `backups` disk.
**Default implemented:** `RequestDataExportAction::WEEKLY_LIMIT` = 5 requests
per tenant per rolling 7 days (429 `EXPORT_WEEKLY_LIMIT_REACHED` past that);
`GenerateDataExportJob::RETENTION_DAYS` = 7 days after completion, after which
the new `data-exports:expire` scheduled command (daily at 04:30) deletes the
S3 object and flips the row to `expired`. Both are named constants, not
scattered literals, so either number can move without an audit of call sites.
**Needs confirmation:** are 5/week and a 7-day retention window right for
pilot practices doing a real GDPR export or an offboarding, or should either
be larger/smaller?

## OQ-12 — Inventory counts: no backend at all yet (UI-17 skipped)
**Raised:** S7 UI queue, UI-17, 2026-07-27.
**Context:** Unlike every other UI-XX item so far, `inventory_counts` has no
migration, model, Action, DTO, policy, or API route anywhere — not a missing
screen over an existing capability, but the whole feature undesigned. Building
even a read-only screen would mean inventing the count-session lifecycle
(who can start/close one, whether closing a count auto-writes an Adjustment
movement per discrepant line via `AdjustStockAction` or requires a separate
confirm step, whether partial/per-location counts are allowed) with no brief
guidance to anchor a "safe default" to.
**Default implemented:** none — asked instead of guessing (per the per-task
contract's step 2). User chose to skip UI-17 for now and continue the queue
(UI-18 onward), deferring counts until its backend is designed as its own
item.
**Needs confirmation:** the count-session lifecycle and reconciliation rule
above, before any migration/Action is written for this domain.

## OQ-11 — tenant_user/invitations/personal_access_tokens still have no
Postgres-level RLS
**Raised:** S5-ANA-03 (Backups), 2026-07-26, while proving a real restore
against the live container surfaced this by accident (see the S5-ANA-03
commit for the two bugs that same proof caught and fixed).
**Context:** `2026_07_25_000001_add_row_level_security_to_tenant_tables
.php`'s own docblock flagged this back in S1-ANA-01: these three tables
carry a `tenant_id` but are resolved *during* authentication, before any
"current tenant" exists to scope by — "RLS on those needs a policy shaped
around that bootstrap lookup... not guessed at here." That policy design
was never actually done in a later sprint; these three tables are still
the only tenant-owned ones relying solely on manual query-level scoping
in the Identity domain's actions, not a second line of defence.
**Default implemented:** nothing changed here this round — the actual bug
this session's live-restore proof caught and fixed
(`App\Support\Tenancy\TenantContext`) was a different, narrower problem:
`roles`/`model_has_roles`/`model_has_permissions` (which *do* have RLS,
added in S1-ANA-03) were being written to during registration/invitation
-acceptance before anything bound `app.tenant_id`, and every automated
test masked it by running under the elevated DB role instead of the
restricted one the app actually uses.
**Needs confirmation:** should tenant_user/invitations/personal_access_
tokens get real RLS policies now (shaped around the bootstrap lookups
that must work before a tenant is "current" — e.g. USING (true) for
SELECT during login/invitation-token lookup, but a real policy for
writes), or is the existing manual-scoping-only approach an accepted
risk for these specific three tables?

## OQ-10 — Staging/monitoring: no infrastructure exists yet
**Raised:** S5-ANA-02 (Operations), 2026-07-26
**Context:** the backlog asks for "staging, logs, monitoring, alerts" —
but no staging host, domain, Sentry project, or (if different from
MinIO) managed S3/mail account exists yet. None of that is something to
invent; it needs an actual decision about where this runs.
**Default implemented:** everything that's pure code/config, so it's
ready the moment real infrastructure exists: sentry/sentry-laravel wired
into `bootstrap/app.php` (no-ops with a blank DSN — see `.env.staging
.example`), the existing `stderr` log channel (already the production
default since S0, works with any external log collector that tails
container output), and `docker-compose.staging.yml` — a skeleton mirroring
local dev's service topology (self-hosted Postgres/Redis/MinIO, no
Mailpit — real Resend mail) with no host port mappings on the data
services and no anonymous MinIO access, unlike local dev's convenience
defaults.
**Not implemented / needs a decision:** where staging actually runs (a
single VM? a managed container platform?), TLS termination and the real
domain (FrankenPHP serves plain HTTP on :8000 — something in front has to
terminate TLS), a Sentry account/project, and who gets alerted for
queue/capacity/certificate problems and how (Sentry alerts? something
else?). `docker-compose.staging.yml`'s header comment lists these
explicitly.
**Update (S6):** `docs/deployment.md`'s "Production deploy runbook"
section is now a full checklist (pre-flight, deploy, post-deploy
verification, rollback) written against what exists today, so the first
real rehearsal is "follow these steps" rather than inventing a procedure
from scratch — but it is still unrehearsed against a real target, since
none of the infrastructure above exists yet.

## OQ-9 — Non-conformities: no un-recall/un-quarantine path, no type taxonomy
**Raised:** S4-ANA-05 (Non-conformities), 2026-07-26
**Context:** CLAUDE.md invariant #3 promises "a non_conformity + recall,
never by UPDATE" but doesn't specify what happens *after* — whether a
recalled label or quarantined batch can ever be cleared back to normal
use, and under what authority. It also doesn't give a controlled
vocabulary for non-conformity types/categories.
**Default implemented:** raising a non-conformity against a cycle or
label recalls the affected label(s) (and quarantines any linked batch)
immediately and irreversibly via this codebase — there is no
un-recall/un-quarantine action at all yet. `description` is free text,
no `type` enum. Resolving a non-conformity only records a resolution
note; it does not reverse the recall/quarantine.
**Needs confirmation:** should a resolved non-conformity ever be able to
restore a label/batch to normal use (and if so, requiring what evidence
— a second sign-off? a lab retest record?), and is a fixed type taxonomy
needed for reporting (e.g. "equipment failure" vs "release error" vs
"control test failure")?

## OQ-8 — No seeded EN 868 default DLU rules
**Raised:** S3-ANA-04 (Labels), 2026-07-26
**Context:** CLAUDE.md says DLU "comes from a per-tenant rule table
(packaging x storage, EN 868 defaults)." EN 868 doesn't itself mandate a
single shelf-life number per packaging/storage combination — actual
practice varies (event-related vs time-related storage, specific pouch
material, sealed cupboard vs open shelf), and guessing concrete day counts
here would mean inventing a compliance figure, not implementing a safe
default.
**Default implemented:** the `dlu_rules` table + full CRUD
(`labels.manage`), keyed on `(tenant_id, packaging_type, storage_condition)`
→ `shelf_life_days`, with **no rows seeded**. Generating labels for a
released cycle (`POST /cycles/{cycle}/labels`) requires the caller to name
a packaging_type/storage_condition that already has a matching rule —
`DLU_RULE_NOT_FOUND` (422) if not, never a silent fallback number. Once
matched, the rule's shelf_life_days is frozen onto every label it produces,
so a later edit to the rule never rewrites already-printed evidence.
**Needs confirmation:** what packaging/storage categories and day counts
this practice (and, longer-term, a shipped "EN 868 defaults" starter set)
should actually use.
**UI-28 (2026-07-28):** the DLU rule table now has a settings-page editor,
but still seeds nothing — inventing concrete day counts here would still
mean inventing a compliance figure, exactly this question's original
reasoning. The section shows a persistent banner instead: shelf-life
values are unverified until a dental professional signs them off, and no
defaults are pre-filled. Still open.

## OQ-7 — Control tests: attached to a production cycle, or their own
daily log?
**Raised:** S3-ANA-02 (Cycles, loads, control tests), 2026-07-26
**Context:** CLAUDE.md calls for a "control-test logbook
(vacuum/Bowie-Dick/Helix/biological) with missing-test alerts." In real
sterilization practice, Bowie-Dick and Helix tests are typically run once
a day as their *own* dedicated empty-chamber cycle, before any production
load — not attached to an arbitrary load of instruments. A vacuum test is
part of every cycle's own program; a biological indicator is usually
seeded into a production load and read later.
**Default implemented:** `control_tests` rows always belong to a specific
`cycle_id` (any type, any cycle) — the simplest model that satisfies "a
logbook of tests per cycle," recordable any time from `Completed` through
`AwaitingRelease` (not locked immediately at submission, since a
biological indicator's result can take 24-48h to incubate and legitimately
arrives later). A cycle with a `Fail` result immediately opens a
`failed_cycle` alert (unambiguous — no rule to invent there).
**Not implemented:** the `missing_test` alert type from CLAUDE.md's alert
list — flagging "no Bowie-Dick test recorded today" requires deciding
required test frequency (daily? per device? per tenant?), which is a
regulatory rule, not a default to guess. `AlertType::MissingTest` doesn't
exist yet; only `FailedCycle` was added this round.
**Needs confirmation:** should Bowie-Dick/Helix instead be modeled as a
standalone daily log independent of any specific production cycle, and
what the actual required test frequency/type-per-device-kind rules are —
that second answer is also what `missing_test` needs before it can be
built without inventing a compliance rule.
**UI-30 addendum, 2026-07-29:** the dashboard's attention queue would have
included "control tests overdue or due today" — skipped for the same
reason (`AlertSettings.control_test_frequency_days`/
`control_test_overdue_tolerance_days` are still stored but never read by
any detection logic), per explicit user decision, same precedent as UI-17
(inventory counts).

## OQ-6 — Near-expiry alert window
**Raised:** S2-ANA-05 (Alert engine), 2026-07-28
**Context:** Nothing in the brief specifies how many days before a batch's
expiry (DLU-adjacent, but this is the *stock* expiry alert, not the label
DLU rule) a near-expiry alert should fire.
**Default implemented:** 30 days (`DetectAlertsAction::DEFAULT_NEAR_EXPIRY_DAYS`),
hardcoded, not yet per-tenant configurable.
**Needs confirmation:** is 30 days right, and should this eventually be a
per-tenant setting (packaging/storage-dependent, like the DLU rule table
CLAUDE.md describes for labels) rather than a single constant?
**Resolved by UI-28 (2026-07-28):** it's now a real per-tenant setting
(`AlertSettings.near_expiry_days`, Practice Settings > Alerts &
Notifications), 30 days is still the default for a tenant that's never
changed it. The "is 30 days right" question itself is still open — a
practice can now answer it for themselves.

## OQ-5 — Audit log "UI viewer" is API-only; the web app has no tenant
resolution yet
**Raised:** S1-ANA-04 (Audit log), 2026-07-25
**Context:** The backlog item asks for the audit log plus a UI viewer.
Everything shipped so far — S1-ANA-01 through S1-ANA-04 — is the
`/api/v1` surface the mobile app (and, indirectly, an Inertia frontend)
consumes; the token-scoped tenant resolution it relies on
(`App\Http\Middleware\Api\SetCurrentTenant`, reading the Sanctum token)
has no web/session equivalent. The web app currently authenticates via
Fortify exactly as the starter kit shipped it — a single global session
with no concept of "which practice" at all. NAMING.md's subdomain
convention (`{slug}.steriqore.<tld>`) implies the web side should resolve
tenant by subdomain rather than by token, which is a different mechanism
from the API's and not yet built.
**Default implemented:** `GET /api/v1/audit-events` — real, tested, permission
-gated (owner/admin only), tenant-scoped. No Inertia page renders it.
Building one now, ahead of web-side tenant resolution existing, would mean
either a page with no real tenant scoping (a security bug) or reinventing
that resolution ad hoc for one page instead of deciding it properly.
**Needs confirmation:** should web tenant resolution be subdomain-based (matches
NAMING.md) — its own backlog item — before any Inertia/React page (audit
log or otherwise) is built against tenant-scoped data?

## OQ-4 — Sanctum token lifetime
**Raised:** S1-ANA-02 (Identity), 2026-07-25
**Context:** Nothing in the brief specifies how long a mobile session/token
should last before requiring re-login.
**Default implemented:** `config('sanctum.expiration')` = 30 days
(`SANCTUM_TOKEN_EXPIRATION_MINUTES` env override), enforced by Sanctum's
guard against each token's `created_at`. Revocation (logout, logout-everywhere,
disabling a membership) is immediate regardless of this TTL.
**Needs confirmation:** is 30 days right for the pilot, or should it be
shorter given this is health-adjacent data?

## OQ-3 — Migrating `users.id` from bigint to uuid touches a completed item
**Raised:** S0-ANA-02 (ERD), 2026-07-24
**Context:** S0-ANA-01 (repo skeleton) is marked Completed and shipped a
starter-kit `users` table with a bigint auto-increment `id`. The tenancy
invariant requires UUIDv7 ids everywhere. Bringing `users` in line means a
migration that changes its primary key type and updates the `passkeys.user_id`
FK.
**Default implemented:** done — edited the original `0001_01_01_000000` and
`passkeys` migrations in place (not yet run against any shared/prod DB, so no
data was at risk) to bring `users.id` to `uuid` with the same UUIDv7 pattern
as every other table. `ProfileValidationRules::profileRules()`'s `?int
$userId` parameter was widened to `?string` to match — the only call site
that assumed a bigint id.
**Needs confirmation:** OK that this was done without waiting, given it was a
hard blocker for every other table's FKs? Flag if bigint ids on `users`
specifically were kept for a reason not visible in the code.

## OQ-2 — Tenant plan/status values and trial length
**Raised:** S0-ANA-02 (ERD), 2026-07-24
**Context:** `tenants.plan`/`tenants.status` need a concrete enum. Billing is
out of MVP scope, so this is a minimal placeholder. The brief says "15–30 day
self-serve trial" without picking a number, and doesn't define what a
`suspended` tenant should actually be blocked from.
**Default implemented:** `plan`: `trial`/`active`/`suspended`. `status`:
`trialing`/`active`/`suspended`/`cancelled`. `trial_ends_at` nullable
timestamp, no default length enforced in the schema (set at tenant-creation
time in code).
**Needs confirmation:** exact trial length in days, and the precise behaviour
of `suspended` (read-only? fully locked? grace period?).

## OQ-1 — Can a user belong to more than one tenant?
**Raised:** S0-ANA-02 (ERD), 2026-07-24
**Context:** The build brief's domain model lists a `tenant_user` pivot
(implying many-to-many between users and tenants), which would matter for a
locum dentist working across multiple practices. But the tenancy invariant
("the tenant never comes from a request parameter — only from the
session/token") only holds cleanly if each authenticated session/token
resolves to exactly one tenant.
**Default implemented:** schema allows multi-membership at the data level
(`tenant_user` many-to-many), but authentication is single-tenant per
session/token — a user with two memberships logs in once per tenant and gets
a separate session/Sanctum token per tenant, chosen at login. Switching
practice requires re-authenticating, never a mid-session tenant switch.
**Needs confirmation:** does this match the intended workflow, or should the
MVP simply forbid multi-tenant membership altogether (one user = one practice,
full stop) until there's a real need for it?

==================== ./docs/operations.md ====================

# Operations

## Scheduled jobs

Defined in `routes/console.php`, run by the `scheduler` process inside
the container (`php artisan schedule:work`):

| Job | Schedule | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `horizon:snapshot` | every 5 minutes | Queue metrics for the Horizon dashboard |
| `alerts:detect` | hourly | Low-stock / near-expiry / expired-batch alerts, per tenant |
| `backup:run --only-db` | daily at 02:00 | PostgreSQL dump → `steriqore-backups` bucket |
| `steriqore:backup-media` | daily at 02:10 | Mirrors every file on the `media` disk to `backups` |
| `backup:clean` | daily at 03:00 | Prunes old backups per `config/backup.php`'s retention rules |
| `backup:monitor` | daily at 04:00 | Alerts if backups are missing, too old, or too large (`config/backup.php`) |

Set `RUN_SCHEDULER=false` on any replica that shouldn't run these (the
scheduler process becomes `sleep infinity` instead).

## Backups and restore

Two independent backups run nightly, both landing on the `backups` disk
(`steriqore-backups` bucket):

1. **Database** — `spatie/laravel-backup`'s `pg_dump`, via the
   `pgsql_admin` connection specifically (`config/backup.php`). The
   restricted `steriqore_app` role that the app actually runs as cannot
   do a full-database dump: Row-Level Security blocks any query that
   isn't scoped to a single tenant, and a whole-database backup isn't
   scoped to one.
2. **Media files** — `App\Domain\Compliance\Actions
   \MirrorMediaBackupAction` copies every object from the `media` disk
   to `backups/media-backup/`, preserving its path (`spatie/laravel
   -backup`'s own file-backup feature only zips local paths, and the
   real user-generated files — cycle attachments — live on S3/MinIO).

### Restoring

**Database** — download the dump, then:

```bash
unzip <backup>.zip -d extracted
psql "postgresql://<user>:<pass>@<host>:5432/<database>" -f extracted/db-dumps/postgresql-<db>.sql
```

**Media files** — reverse the mirror:

```bash
php artisan tinker --execute="app(App\Domain\Compliance\Actions\RestoreMediaBackupAction::class)->execute();"
```

Both directions were verified for real against the live Docker
environment while building this (S5-ANA-03): a real `pg_dump`, a real
restore into a scratch database with a just-registered tenant and its
roles intact, and a real file deleted from `media` and fully recovered
from `backups`.

### A note on how this was actually proven

Running the real restore (not just asserting it works) caught two bugs
that every automated test had missed, because the test suite's default
database connection is deliberately the elevated migrations role (see
`phpunit.xml`'s comment) — it never exercised the restricted role the
app actually runs as for these code paths:

- `league/flysystem-aws-s3-v3` was never installed, so every S3
  operation would have failed in a real environment.
- Registering a tenant or accepting an invitation wrote to RLS-protected
  tables (`roles`, `model_has_roles`) before anything had bound "the
  current tenant" — fixed via `App\Support\Tenancy\TenantContext`.

Both are fixed (with a regression test for the second). The lesson this
leaves for future ops work: **anything that touches infrastructure this
directly (backups, restores, real S3, real Postgres roles) deserves at
least one manual, real-environment rehearsal — automated tests running
under an elevated role can hide exactly this class of bug.**

## Monitoring

- **Errors** — Sentry (`sentry/sentry-laravel`), wired into
  `bootstrap/app.php`. No-ops with a blank `SENTRY_LARAVEL_DSN`; set a
  real one in `.env.staging`/production once a Sentry project exists.
  `send_default_pii` stays `false` given how strict CLAUDE.md is about
  patient-data pseudonymization — don't change this without a written
  decision.
- **Queues** — Horizon dashboard at `/horizon`.
- **Logs** — `stderr` channel (the production default since S0); works
  with any log collector that tails container output.
- **Capacity / certificates** — not yet wired to anything; no monitoring
  service or hosting platform is decided (`docs/open-questions.md`
  OQ-10).

## Rate limits

Two named limiters (`app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php`):

- **`public-api`** — 10/minute per IP. Applied to the three
  unauthenticated endpoints: tenant registration, login, invitation
  acceptance. The brute-force/spam surface.
- **`api`** — 120/minute per authenticated user (falls back to IP).
  Everything else.

A 429 response means the limit was hit — check whether it's a genuine
abuse pattern or a client retrying too aggressively before raising it.

## Idempotency

Every mutating endpoint requires an `Idempotency-Key` header (400 if
missing). The server stores the key + a hash of the request + its
response for 24h (`app/Http/Middleware/Api/EnsureIdempotency.php`) and
replays it verbatim on an exact repeat — a `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`
means the same key was sent with a *different* request body, which
usually indicates a client bug (reusing a key across genuinely different
requests), not a server problem.

## Common troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| A route 404s that should exist | `SetCurrentTenant` middleware priority — check `bootstrap/app.php`'s `prependToPriorityList`. If it runs after `SubstituteBindings`, every route with an implicitly-bound tenant-scoped model 404s (TenantScope fails closed with no tenant bound yet). |
| RLS error on an insert/update from application code | Something is writing to a tenant-scoped table without the tenant bound first (`app.tenant_id` unset). Check whether the code path runs before `SetCurrentTenant` (or `App\Support\Tenancy\TenantContext` for the two bootstrap exceptions: registration, invitation acceptance). |
| Code changes don't take effect in the running container | Octane keeps the app booted in memory across requests — `docker compose cp` alone isn't enough. Restart the app service (`./steriqore.sh restart`) or use `docker compose watch` (`sync+restart` in `docker-compose.yml`), which does this automatically. |
| A file upload/PDF render fails only in the container, works in tests | The test suite uses `Storage::fake()`/`Pdf::fake()` for S3 and Browsershot — neither actually exercises the real driver. Verify manually against the running container if either changes. |


==================== ./docs/performance.md ====================

# Performance at pilot volume (S5-ANA-04)

CLAUDE.md's targets: "Common screens < 2s; evidence search < 2s at pilot
volume (index deliberately, GIN/tsvector)." REC-09: "search by
patient/cycle/batch -> complete result < 2s at pilot volume."

"Pilot volume" isn't given an exact number anywhere in the brief, so this
picks a concrete, documented scale rather than leaving the target
untested against any real figure — roughly one busy single-practice
year: **3 devices, 3,000 cycles, 10 pouches/cycle (30,000 labels/label
usages), 2,000 patients, 500 batches**. Generated via
`php artisan steriqore:seed-pilot-volume` (`app/Console/Commands
/SeedPilotVolume.php`) — bulk SQL inserts, not the API, so seeding itself
takes seconds rather than being part of what's timed.

## Method

Measured against the real Docker stack (not the test suite, which uses
an in-memory/local setup for speed) — a real HTTP request, through Sanctum
auth and the `tenant` middleware, to the running Octane/FrankenPHP
container, hitting real PostgreSQL 18.

## Results

| Request | Time |
|---|---|
| `GET /evidence-search` (no filter, worst case) | 44ms |
| `GET /evidence-search?patient_reference=...` | 19ms |
| `GET /evidence-search?batch_number=...` | 18ms |
| `GET /evidence-search?cycle_number=...` | 16ms |
| `GET /evidence-search?from=...&to=...` (full window) | 17ms |
| `GET /evidence-search/export?format=xlsx` (last 30 days, ~250 rows) | 83ms |
| `GET /evidence-search/export?format=xlsx` (all 30,000 rows) | 7.1s |
| `GET /cycles` | 13ms |
| `GET /patients` | 9ms |

Every *search* path is roughly 100x under the 2s target. `EXPLAIN
ANALYZE` on the underlying queries confirms every filter (patient
reference, cycle number, batch number, device, date range) resolves via
an index scan, never a sequential scan — the `label_usages
(tenant_id, used_at)` and `cycle_items.batch_id` indexes added in
S4-ANA-03, plus the existing unique constraints that double as indexes
on their leading columns (`cycles (tenant_id, device_id, cycle_number)`,
`cycle_items (cycle_id, sequence_in_cycle)`, `labels.cycle_item_id`,
`label_usages.label_id`).

GIN/tsvector was deliberately not added anywhere: every filter here is an
exact or prefix match on a structured column, not free-text search —
plain btree is the correct index type for this filter set, not a
full-text one.

## The one number outside target: full-history export

Exporting *all 30,000 rows* in one XLSX takes ~7 seconds — outside the
2s target, but the target is explicitly for *search*, not bulk exports,
and a realistic export (a date-bounded range, e.g. "last 30 days" — 83ms
for ~250 rows) is nowhere near it. Flagged here rather than silently
building a queued/async export nobody asked for: **if a tenant is
expected to routinely export their entire multi-year history in one
request, that likely needs `Excel::queue()` instead of the current
`Excel::download()`** (spatie/laravel-backup and Horizon are both
already in the stack for this) — not implemented, since nothing in
CLAUDE.md or the backlog asks for exports specifically to meet the 2s
bar, and doing so would be inventing scope.

## Cleaning up the pilot-volume tenant

The seeded tenant is fully isolated (its own `tenant_id`) and doesn't
interfere with anything else — safe to leave for further exploration, or
remove with:

```sql
delete from tenants where slug like 'pilot-volume-%';
```

(every child table cascades on `tenant_id`, per the existing FK
constraints).


==================== ./docs/ui-backlog.md ====================

# S7 — UI task queue

The app shell is done. Everything else is a "Soon" stub until its item lands
here. Work the queue below **one task at a time** — the user says "Build
UI-XX"; do not start the next until they say so (a terse "processed" /
"process" / "continue" on the current task counts as that signal for the
*next* queued item).

This file is the durable record of that queue: what each item covers, what
got built, and what's still open. Update the **Status** column (and add a
one-line note) as part of every task's commit — CLAUDE.md points here so it
loads every session.

## Per-task contract (all 8 steps, every item)

1. Read the build brief and locate the EXISTING Action(s)/query the screen
   calls. State which ones will be used before writing code.
2. If the screen needs behaviour the domain layer doesn't already have,
   STOP and tell the user. Do not add migrations, invent business rules, or
   widen an Action's scope. Small, safe, mechanical extensions (a filter
   mirroring an existing one, widening a DTO with an existing column) are
   fine to just do and document. A genuine architecture gap ("no creation
   path exists at all") is stop-worthy.
3. Build the Inertia page + components. Props are typed spatie/laravel-data
   DTOs. TypeScript stays strict — no `any`, no `as unknown as`.
4. Every state is designed: loading skeleton, empty state, error state,
   permission-denied case (item simply isn't rendered).
5. Authorization: controller goes through its Policy. Hiding a button is
   UX, never security. Add the route to the permission-aware nav.
6. Remove the "Soon" badge for that nav item and enable the link.
7. Tests: a feature test (happy path + policy denial + cross-tenant
   403/404) and a Playwright happy path. Existing suite stays green.
8. Report: routes added, DTOs, files touched, a screenshot, and anything
   that hit step 2.

## Design constraints (every screen)

- Semantic status color only (icon+text+color, never color alone).
- Tabular numerals aligned in tables; compact rows, sticky headers,
  URL-persisted filters.
- Print stylesheet forcing a light surface.
- Irreversible actions name their consequence in the confirm button/copy.
- Keyboard nav, visible focus, reduced motion respected.
